Search Close Draft ACT Skate Strategy Following a community-driven inquiry with 33 recommendations, the ACT Government is seeking feedback on a Draft Skate Strategy to support planning and skate culture. This project is open for feedback About the Draft ACT Skate Strategy The 2022-2024 Inquiry into Skateboarding and Skateparks in the ACT (the Inquiry) was initiated in response to community petitions. The Inquiry made 33 recommendations for government consideration. One of the recommendations was to develop a Draft ACT Skate Strategy (Draft Strategy), responding to community aspirations for better planning and support for skate culture. The ACT Government has developed a Draft Strategy in collaboration with skating stakeholders, community groups, industry experts and government partners. Now, we are seeking community feedback to help finalise the strategy. The aim of the finalised ACT Skate Strategy will be to deliver a strong framework, clear objectives, practical actions and a pathway for ensuring that skating in the ACT continues to grow in a way that is inclusive, sustainable, strengthens community connection and supports creative expression and wellbeing. The strategy will also support promotion of skate culture in the ACT as well as planning, designing, managing and operating skate infrastructure across the Territory. What we're looking at The Draft Strategy considers future opportunities to deliver safe, inclusive and accessible skate friendly infrastructure in public spaces across Canberra. The goals of the Draft Strategy are to: preserve ACT skateboarding heritage encourage the community to skate provide modern, inclusive and safe skating infrastructure incorporate skating infrastructure into public spaces improve wellbeing and mental health maintain existing skating infrastructure service a variety of skating and recreational activities including street and park skateboarding, scooters, roller blades and BMX. To learn about the objectives, we will use to reach these goals read the Draft ACT Skate Strategy below before completing the survey. How to have your say Read the Draft Strategy and answer the survey below. Alternatively, you can also attend one of our community pop ups as detailed below or send us an email directly. Survey Have your say on the Draft ACT Skate Strategy. Complete the survey Community pop ups Saturday 5 September 2026, 2pm - 4pm at Woden Skatepark, 50 Launceston Street, Phillip. Saturday 19 September 2026, 10am - 12pm at Belconnen Skatepark, 50 Emu Bank Belconnen. Saturday 3 October 2026, 10am - 12pm at Tuggeranong Skatepark, 25 Bartlet Place, Greenway. Email us Email your feedback to communityengagement@act.gov.au. Send us an email Frequently Asked Questions ​What will be the outcome of the Draft Strategy? ​Will the Draft Strategy only focus on skateparks? What is not included in the Draft Strategy? ​When will the ACT Government release the final ACT Skate Strategy? Frequently Asked Questions ​What will be the outcome of the Draft Strategy? The Draft ACT Skate Strategy will provide a clear vision, objectives and desired outcomes for skating and associated skate park infrastructure in the ACT. It will be able to inform decision making on the outcomes identified in the Draft Strategy. ​Will the Draft Strategy only focus on skateparks? No. The Draft Strategy will consider all skating and recreational activities including street and park skateboarding, scooters, roller blades and BMX. The Draft Strategy focuses on skating as a sport and more broadly, a recreational activity the community can be involved in and connected to. What is not included in the Draft Strategy? Private indoor facilities, BMX-only tracks, playgrounds, nature play spaces, learn-to-ride tracks, outdoor fitness equipment, areas with skate deterrents, unrelated facilities and infrastructure audits. ​When will the ACT Government release the final ACT Skate Strategy? Once endorsed by Cabinet, the final ACT Skate Strategy will be released in 2026. Close The impact of having your say The ACT Government will consider all feedback and will use it to finalise the Draft Strategy for submission to Cabinet. After the strategy is finalised it will be published on the City Services website and the ACT Government will use it to inform decision making on recommendations for future works to deliver on the outcomes identified in the Draft Strategy. Privacy YourSay Privacy Statement This site is owned and operated by the ACT Government using software licensed from Social Pinpoint. For details on how the ACT Government collects and protects your personal information, refer to their Privacy Policy below. For details of how Social Pinpoint may access personal information, please refer to Social Pinpoint’s Privacy Policy . The online 'YourSay' service is provided using a digital platform operated by the Chief Minister, Treasury and Economic Development Directorate (CMTEDD). The ACT Government respects the rights and privacy of all individuals and is committed to complying with the Information Privacy Act 2014 and the Territory Privacy Principles and protecting the personal information we hold. This Privacy Policy describes how the ACT Government collects and uses your personal information collected through the ‘YourSay’ website. Defined terms appear in bold and definitions appear at the end of the Statement. Why does the ACT Government collect personal information, and how is it used? CMTEDD (via Social Pinpoint which is contracted service provider of CMTEDD) collects your personal information as part of providing the Territory’s online community engagement services, informing you about these services, complying with contractual and other legal obligations, responding to your enquiries and administering its community engagement technology. CMTEDD may use your personal information for these purposes, any other purpose listed on a collection statement at the point of collection, or in any other way made clear at the time of collecting the personal information . In cases where feedback is received about an engagement opportunity that is subject to another Territory agency's Terms and Conditions, or arrangements for handling personal information , your feedback may be provided to the agency concerned. In your feedback to the ACT Government, you should not provide personal information , including personal health information (for example, any information (medical or otherwise) about a person’s health, mental status, treatments received etc) about any other person (a third person). What information do we collect about you? User feedback We collect the comments, votes, posts and selections you contribute when interacting with the feedback mechanisms provided through 'YourSay', which include: forums interactive maps surveys quick polls This information is analysed and interpreted by CMTEDD staff, staff of other ACT Government agencies and in some circumstances, third party contractors who have been engaged to assist in the analysis of the data collected, to inform the creation of better projects, plans and policies. Can you remain anonymous or withhold personal information? Yes. You can access and participate in select ‘YourSay’ engagements anonymously, without disclosing any personal information . Some identified studies may require you to register and establish an account in order to participate. Users may choose to adopt a pseudonym for these studies. Registered Users When you register for a ‘YourSay’ account or sign-in to your existing account, the information we may collect includes: first and last name username (this may be published on the site alongside any public comments you make) email address (this will not be made public) age group gender the region in which you live sign-up date last login date last contribution number of contributions For engagements where you do not register for a ‘YourSay’ account, we may seek to collect from you: username (this is published on the site alongside any public comments you make) email address (this will not be made public) age group gender postcode Demographic details are requested in order to help us determine the degree to which views of participants are representative of a diverse cross-section of the community. By providing an email address you help us protect the integrity of the discussion from individuals and groups who may attempt to unduly influence the outcomes of the consultation process anonymously. For example, we check the database to ensure each user has a single email account on the site. We also frequently review the site for trolls and spammers. If you are registered and signed-in to your user account, the contributions and feedback you provide may be linked with your username and any demographic details you have recorded in your account. Email notifications If you subscribe to receive notifications about upcoming consultations and other engagement activities , the email address you provide will be used by CMTEDD to send you information and updates about new opportunities to have your say. You can unsubscribe from these updates notifications at any time. If you subscribe to receive updates about a specific engagement project, for example by using the ‘Follow’ function, the email address you provide will be used to send you information and updates about that engagement. You can unsubscribe from these notifications at any time. Cookies Cookies are used on our site, but they do not collect any personal information . For the most part they are sessional and just contain system-generated values to identify the user's session for statistical and system administration purposes only. For more information on Cookies and Google Analytics, please refer to the CMTEDD Privacy Policy . Site visit data The site’s web-server automatically collects the following de-identified data for statistical and system administration purposes only: your server (or IP) address the day and time you visited the site the pages you visited on our site the address of the last page you visited the operating system you are using rough geographic location (down to the city) language (e.g. American English) internet service provider (e.g. Telstra) the type of browser and version you are using. To the extent that this data could make you identifiable, CMTEDD and Social Pinpoint will not attempt to identify individuals from the records the server automatically generates unless necessary to investigate a breach of law or regulation. Who has access to information that is collected from you? When you sign up for and use the ‘YourSay’ service you provide two types of information: information that is publicly available; and information that is available to CMTEDD and Social Pinpoint in its capacity as CMTEDD’s contracted service provider (and its agents and sub-contractors who may be based overseas, namely, in the Philippines) and which may be made available by CMTEDD to other entities as set out in this privacy notice. Publicly available information Publicly available information is limited to your username and any comments you leave under that username in the forums or other feedback tools published to ‘YourSay’. You can use your first name or an anonymous username if you do not want your full name attached to forum and guestbook comments, stories or questions. Feedback (including overall results of polls and surveys, and in some instances, quotes from forums and surveys) may be published in publicly available reports at the end of the consultation period. Please note that the ACT Government is subject to the Freedom of Information Act 2016 . The Freedom of Information Act 2016 provides a general right of access to government information. This includes documents created by the government, documents held by contracted service providers relating to the performance of government contracts and documents supplied to government by external organisations or individuals. Information available to CMTEDD and Social Pinpoint (and which CMTEDD may disclose to other entities as set out in this privacy notice) includes : all information from the sign-up form comments, questions, stories, guestbook posts survey responses, quick poll responses, map pins general site activity such as document downloads, videos viewed, images viewed information on the technology used to access the site. Information available to third party contractors may include but is not limited to : comments, questions, stories, guestbook posts survey responses, quick poll responses, map pins de-identified data for reporting purposes. Disclosure of personal information CMTEDD will take all reasonable measures to prevent unauthorised access to, or disclosure of, your personal information . Organisations to which personal information is disclosed include other ACT Government directorates, the ACT Government’s contracted Service Providers, such as Social Pinpoint and their subcontractors or agents who may be based in Australia or overseas (namely in the Philippines), who perform various services for and on behalf of the ACT Government. These contractors have agreed to be bound by the provisions of the Information Privacy Act 2014 . We will also take all necessary measures to ensure that your personal information is not disclosed to other individuals, institutions and authorities except in accordance with the Information Privacy Act 2014 , such as if required or authorised by law or explicitly permitted by you. Some examples of when information may be provided to another person without your consent include in the event of an investigation into suspected unlawful or improper activity or when a law enforcement agency or government agency may exercise its legal authority to inspect the web server's records (e.g. in relation to hacking or abusive messages). Access and correction You may seek corrections to your personal information that CMTEDD has collected if you believe it is inaccurate, out-of–date, incomplete, irrelevant or misleading. CMTEDD is required to take reasonable steps to correct personal information to ensure that, having regard to the purpose for which it is held, the information is not inaccurate, out-of–date, incomplete, irrelevant or misleading. You may also seek access to your personal information that CMTEDD holds. More information about seeking access to, and correction of, your personal information held by CMTEDD can be found in the CMTEDD Information Privacy Policy . Links The ‘YourSay’ Privacy Statement does not apply to third party websites or digital services which may be linked to from content published to 'YourSay'. We recommend you read the privacy statement of the relevant service when you access these sites. Third Party Providers We sometimes use third party providers for some web-based services, with information stored in the United States and Europe. These include Campaign Monitor and Mail Chimp for email subscriptions, Survey Monkey and Typeform for online surveys, Social Pinpoint for interactive maps, Viostream for live streaming question and answers, MindHive for running a collaborative forum and EventBrite for registration at events. Please follow the hyperlinks for details on their privacy policies. Campaign Monitor Privacy CMTEDD uses Campaign Monitor to provide electronic newsletters to subscribers. In distributing newsletters, CMTEDD, via Campaign Monitor, will collect personal information from you, including email addresses you have provided to CMTEDD for the purpose of receiving electronic newsletters, all information relating to those email addresses, and in some cases your name. Campaign Monitor also uses cookies, web beacons and Flash player codes to collect information for use by CMTEDD about: when you access CMTEDD or other ACT Government electronic newsletters your browser type and version your operating system and other similar information your IP address and its geolocation clicks on email links and whether the email is forwarded. CMTEDD holds the Campaign Monitor account and personal information collected through that account can be accessed by other agencies of the ACT Government for the purposes of sending electronic newsletters. For additional detail about the information Campaign Monitor will collect, please refer to Campaign Monitor’s Privacy Policy and Campaign Monitor’s Terms of Use . Campaign Monitor will use the information collected from you for the purpose of providing the online service which enables CMTEDD and other agencies of the ACT Government to create, send and manage electronic newsletters. Campaign Monitor will also use this information to measure the performance of CMTEDD and other ACT Government email campaigns. Campaign Monitor may transfer this information to its contractors or other third parties who process the information on Campaign Monitor’s behalf, or where otherwise required to do so by law. Campaign Monitor is based in the United States of America (USA) and is subject to the laws of the USA. Your information (including your IP address) will be transmitted to and stored by Campaign Monitor on servers located outside Australia. You can unsubscribe from the 'YourSay' electronic newsletter at any time by selecting the 'unsubscribe’ option in every email sent to you by Campaign Monitor. More information about how CMTEDD manages the personal information it collects can be found at https://www.act.gov.au/directorates-and-agencies/chief-minister-treasury-and-economic-development-directorate/cmtedd-privacy . If you have any questions relating to the use of your personal data please contact askus@yoursay.act.gov.au . Whole of Government Engagement Customer Relationship Management System If you provide your personal information during an engagement, it may be included in a Whole of Government Customer Relationship Management System (CRM), together with the feedback or views you provide, and handled in accordance with Schedule 1 of the Information Privacy Act 2014, and the Territory Privacy Principles (TPPs). The CRM system has been designed to provide directorates’ employees or authorised contractors with a place to store information about engagements with stakeholders and access information about engagements with stakeholders undertaken by other employees or authorised contractors. Information in the CRM may be used to inform subsequent engagements with the same or similar stakeholders. The use of the database is intended to strengthen coordination between ACT Public Sector agencies and reduce duplication of effort and stakeholder fatigue, by sharing information about engagement activities across government. More detailed information about how your personal information is handled is available in the CRM Privacy Notice available at https://www.act.gov.au/privacy . Further information about directorates’ privacy policies and where to locate them can be found in the CRM Privacy Notice. Follow This project is open for feedback Canberra is growing — and how we plan for that growth matters. We’re preparing a long-term plan for the Southern Gateway corridor, which extends from Parliament House to Farrer. About the project The Draft Southern Gateway Planning and Design Framework ( the Framework ) is a long-term plan that sets out a vision for how this corridor, extending from Parliament House to Farrer, could develop over the coming decades. It looks ahead to 2050 and beyond, guiding how new homes, transport, jobs, green spaces and community facilities come together in a coordinated way and how new development can respect and enhance the qualities you value most while delivering homes. The Framework uses a vision-led approach, beginning with a big picture vision for the corridor and working down to the details. The Framework comprises the following elements: Vision – A shared vision for the whole corridor, informed by community feedback and the corridor’s current conditions and future opportunities. The vision sets the direction to guide how the corridor will grow and change to 2050 and beyond. The vision for the framework is outlined below: The Southern Gateway to the National Capital will provide more housing in walkable neighbourhoods supported by commercial activity in vibrant urban villages, close to rapid public transport connections, high-quality landscapes, and community and recreational facilities. Principles – The principles set out the concepts for how the vision can be achieved. They are based on existing ACT planning and transport policy, and set out what matters most, like better transport, green spaces and housing choice, and will guide decisions across the entire corridor. Planning and design moves – The practical ideas for how the principles can be applied in the corridor to bring the vision to life. The Framework includes planning and design moves at the whole-of-corridor, precinct, and place scale. The vision brings together land use and transport planning to create more liveable neighbourhoods that focus on: More homes in well-located areas Better transport and connections Thriving centres and employment areas Greener places Community facilities. A growing population means increasing demand for housing, transport and community infrastructure. Planning ahead helps to: Provide more housing in the right locations Reduce urban sprawl Improve travel options Maintain the character and liveability of our neighbourhoods. How to have your say This is your opportunity to help shape the future of the Southern Gateway. The Framework is a draft document and we're seeking community feedback before it is finalised. Your feedback will help ensure the Framework reflects community priorities and supports future planning for the corridor. Your feedback will help: Inform the final Framework. Guide future planning decisions. Influence how neighbourhoods along the Southern Gateway corridor evolve over time. To make the engagement process easier, download the Engagement snapshot document which outlines what you can provide your feedback on and how you can have your say. View upcoming events The project area The Southern Gateway corridor extends from Parliament House to Farrer and encompasses part of the Inner South and Woden districts and includes key centres like Curtin, Mawson and the Woden town centre, and follows major transport routes like Adelaide Avenue, Yarra Glen Drive and Athllon Drive. The Framework divides the corridor into four distinct precincts, each with a unique character and identity. These precincts include: Inner South precinct – includes parts of Yarralumla, Deakin, Barton and Forrest. Yarra Glen precinct – includes west Deakin, Curtin, Hughes and the future north Curtin residential area. Woden precinct – includes Lyons, Chifley and parts of Garran, including Canberra Hospital, as well as the future north Woden development area, the Woden town centre and the Phillip service trades area. Athllon precinct – includes Swinger Hill, Pearce, Torrens, Mawson and Farrer. The study area for the Southern Gateway corridor, including the four precincts, is shown in the map below. What is being proposed The below tiles outline the key areas outlined within the Framework. The ACT Government is releasing the Framework alongside a Southern Gateway Community Needs Assessment so the community can provide feedback on the types of community, sport and recreation facilities needed to support it. More homes in well-located areas A range of housing types More homes close to shops, jobs and rapid transport Better transport and connections Proposed light rail and improved rapid buses Safer walking and cycling connections A more connected, multi-modal corridor Thriving centres and employment areas Vibrant town, group and local centres More jobs, shops and services close to home Walkable urban villages Protecting and enhancing employment areas including west Deakin and the Phillip service trades area Greener places Improved parks and open spaces More trees and shaded areas Enhancements to the Yarralumla Creek corridor Community facilities Planning for future schools, recreation facilities and health services Supporting the needs of a growing population over time A transit-oriented future for Canberra The Framework follows an approach known as transit-oriented development. Transit-oriented development is a way of planning neighbourhoods so that more homes, jobs and everyday services are located close to public transport. The Southern Gateway corridor is already a key transport route, connecting the Inner South and Woden. This approach creates walkable neighbourhoods, where daily needs are close by. This means: More housing density near rapid bus routes and proposed light rail Mid-rise housing near centres, with building heights gradually stepping down to integrate with surrounding suburbs Safer walking and cycling connections Greener streets, parks and public spaces. Transit-oriented development: Makes everyday life easier Provides more options to walk, cycle or use public transport Makes the most of public transport investment Reduces the need to expand into natural areas Creates vibrant communities Provides better access to community facilities and public spaces. FAQ What are the housing opportunities proposed through the Framework? The Framework identifies areas where housing density could increase along the corridor, subject to further investigation. In line with the approach to locate more housing close to shops and rapid transport, new development will generally be focused in existing residential areas within: 800 metres of rapid transport stops 1,000 metres of Woden town centre 800 metres of group centres (Curtin and Mawson) 400 metres of local centres This approach, known as gentle densification, aims to gradually increase housing density in a way that is small-scale, human-centred, and respectful of existing neighbourhood character and walkability. The image below outlines the mix of housing types proposed across the corridor to support population growth and community needs in the areas where it is most appropriate. Mid-rise housing will be concentrated around activity centres and near light rail stops, rapid bus stops, and local and group centres. Building heights will transition down towards established low-rise suburban areas, supporting the government’s commitment to gentle densification. High-rise housing will be limited to Woden town centre. Higher-density development is also suitable for the north Curtin residential area, where there is strong access to transport, services, community facilities, and amenities. Lower-density housing will remain in areas further from centres and rapid transport stops, although many of these locations will still be within walking distance of key destinations. New housing opportunities in the corridor will be delivered gradually over coming decades, responding to the needs of a growing community. Appropriate housing scales within the corridor How will these housing opportunities be implemented? The Framework is a non-statutory document, meaning that while it does not determine outcomes, it will provide direction for future changes to the planning controls along the corridor. Any proposed changes that put the Framework into action will be rolled out gradually, and each stage will include consultation and opportunities for community feedback before decisions are made. What is the Services Trades (CZ3) Technical Paper? The Services Trades (CZ3) Technical Paper is an evidence-based report that examines the role, performance and future of CZ3 (Services) zoned land across the ACT. CZ3 land supports businesses that provide services, trade supplies, storage, logistics and low impact industrial activities, such as vehicle repairs, workshops and small-scale manufacturing. These areas provide important employment opportunities and often offer more affordable commercial space than town centres. The paper reviews how CZ3 areas are performing, identifies opportunities and challenges and provides strategic recommendations to help inform future planning decisions. It includes a detailed assessment of the phillip service trades area, responding to the Minister for Planning's request for further work on the future of the precinct and outlining six planning options for consideration. The technical paper does not change planning policy or zoning. Instead, it provides the evidence and analysis to support future planning work and decision-making. Was a specific Community Needs Assessment conducted for the Southern Gateway? In 2024, the ACT Government commissioned the Community, Sport and Recreation Facilities Needs Assessment and Social Infrastructure Audit , which looked at facility needs across most ACT districts. This was an ACT wide study. Using the information from this audit, a Southern Gateway Community Needs Assessment was prepared to better understand current and future community infrastructure needs across the corridor. Social infrastructure includes the places and services that help people live healthy, connected lives, such as schools, health services, parks, libraries, community centres, meeting places and sporting facilities. The Southern Gateway Community Needs Assessment is being released alongside the Framework to support informed community feedback. The assessment provides an evidence base to support long-term planning and investment. It will help inform conversations with the community and guide future decisions about the type, location and timing of social infrastructure needs to support growth along the corridor. The Southern Gateway Community Needs Assessment helps ensure that planning for the Southern Gateway is not just about housing and transport but also about providing the facilities, services and spaces needed to support a growing and changing community. Read the Southern Gateway Community Needs Assessment . What were the key findings of the Southern Gateway Community Needs Assessment? The Southern Gateway Community Needs Assessment identified several key trends and opportunities: Growing demand : Population growth and increasing density are creating opportunities to expand and enhance community, sport and recreation facilities, particularly in Woden, to support a larger and more active population. An ageing population: There are opportunities to strengthen aged care, health services and integrated models of care that support people to age well within their communities. Expanding community spaces: Demand for spaces that support young people, older residents, arts, culture and flexible community activities presents opportunities to diversify and modernise the community infrastructure network. Sport and recreation growth: Increasing participation in sport and recreation creates opportunities to invest in indoor sports facilities, outdoor courts and youth-oriented recreation spaces, like skate and BMX infrastructure. Education and childcare development: Population growth provides opportunities to expand schools and early childhood services, improve accessibility and support greater provision by not-for-profit providers. Enhancing open spaces: Existing open space assets provide opportunities to improve accessibility, functionality and supporting amenities, such as dog parks and community gardens, to support higher-density within neighbourhoods. Responding to changing community needs: Increasing cultural diversity and evolving household structures create opportunities to deliver more inclusive, accessible and adaptable services, facilities and programs that meet a wider range of community needs. What is a community needs assessment? A Community Needs Assessment is a way of understanding what facilities, services and spaces a community has now, and what it will need in the future. It looks at population growth, existing infrastructure (like community centres, sports facilities and open space) and whether there are any gaps or areas where demand is increasing. It combines data, planning analysis and community input to build a clear picture of local needs. This helps guide decisions about where new facilities are needed, how existing ones can be improved, and how to plan for a growing and changing community so people can continue to live well. For the Southern Gateway Corridor, the needs assessment: Identifies existing community and social infrastructure across the corridor Uses population forecasts, benchmarking and best practice research to understand future needs Considers opportunities to improve access to community infrastructure and coordinate future delivery Helps inform long term planning and investment decisions Provides an evidence base to support community engagement and future planning. How does development occur once the Framework is finalised? Once engagement closes a listening report will be prepared and released to the community. The feedback received will be used to inform the final Framework. Once the final Framework is released, it will guide how the area grows and changes over time. This won’t be the last chance for community input. There will be more opportunities to have your say as planning progresses in the corridor. If planning proposals or changes to planning controls are developed to implement the Framework, they will be consulted on separately through the ACT Planning website in accordance with legislative requirements. Future changes to planning controls and policy The Framework is a strategic planning document that sets out a long-term vision for the corridor to 2050 and beyond. While it does not change planning rules, it will help guide future planning and development decisions. To support this vision, changes to planning controls will be needed through updates to the Territory Plan and, in some areas, the National Capital Plan. The ACT Government and the National Capital Authority will work together on these changes and continue to consult with the community as specific proposals are developed. Updates to the Territory Plan (the ACT's planning “rulebook”) are made through Major Plan Amendments. These amendments can enable significant changes, such as new housing, shops, offices, community facilities and changes to building heights. Key things to know about Major Plan Amendments: Changes will be introduced in stages over time rather than all at once. Each stage will focus on different parts of the corridor, starting with priority areas identified for change. Every Major Plan Amendment includes opportunities for community consultation and feedback before decisions are made. Future Major Plan Amendments and planning proposals will be consulted on separately through the ACT Planning website in accordance with legislative requirements. They are not part of this YourSay consultation. In simple terms, Major Plan Amendments are the process used to update planning rules to support future development. You can learn more about the Territory Plan and Major Plan Amendments by visiting the ACT Planning website . While the Framework does not determine future development outcomes, it will help guide future Major Plan Amendments and also inform the review of District Strategies, which occurs every five years. The online 'YourSay' service is provided using a digital platform operated by the Chief Minister, Treasury and Economic Development Directorate (CMTEDD). The ACT Government respects the rights and privacy of all individuals and is committed to complying with the Information Privacy Act 2014 and the Territory Privacy Principles and protecting the personal information we hold. This Privacy Policy describes how the ACT Government collects and uses your personal information collected through the ‘YourSay’ website. Defined terms appear in bold and definitions appear at the end of the Statement. Why does the ACT Government collect personal information, and how is it used? CMTEDD (via Social Pinpoint which is contracted service provider of CMTEDD) collects your personal information as part of providing the Territory’s online community engagement services, informing you about these services, complying with contractual and other legal obligations, responding to your enquiries and administering its community engagement technology. CMTEDD may use your personal information for these purposes, any other purpose listed on a collection statement at the point of collection, or in any other way made clear at the time of collecting the personal information . In cases where feedback is received about an engagement opportunity that is subject to another Territory agency's Terms and Conditions, or arrangements for handling personal information , your feedback may be provided to the agency concerned. In your feedback to the ACT Government, you should not provide personal information , including personal health information (for example, any information (medical or otherwise) about a person’s health, mental status, treatments received etc) about any other person (a third person). What information do we collect about you? User feedback We collect the comments, votes, posts and selections you contribute when interacting with the feedback mechanisms provided through 'YourSay', which include: forums interactive maps surveys quick polls This information is analysed and interpreted by CMTEDD staff, staff of other ACT Government agencies and in some circumstances, third party contractors who have been engaged to assist in the analysis of the data collected, to inform the creation of better projects, plans and policies. Can you remain anonymous or withhold personal information? Yes. You can access and participate in select ‘YourSay’ engagements anonymously, without disclosing any personal information . Some identified studies may require you to register and establish an account in order to participate. Users may choose to adopt a pseudonym for these studies. Registered Users When you register for a ‘YourSay’ account or sign-in to your existing account, the information we may collect includes: first and last name username (this may be published on the site alongside any public comments you make) email address (this will not be made public) age group gender the region in which you live sign-up date last login date last contribution number of contributions For engagements where you do not register for a ‘YourSay’ account, we may seek to collect from you: username (this is published on the site alongside any public comments you make) email address (this will not be made public) age group gender postcode Demographic details are requested in order to help us determine the degree to which views of participants are representative of a diverse cross-section of the community. By providing an email address you help us protect the integrity of the discussion from individuals and groups who may attempt to unduly influence the outcomes of the consultation process anonymously. For example, we check the database to ensure each user has a single email account on the site. We also frequently review the site for trolls and spammers. If you are registered and signed-in to your user account, the contributions and feedback you provide may be linked with your username and any demographic details you have recorded in your account. Email notifications If you subscribe to receive notifications about upcoming consultations and other engagement activities , the email address you provide will be used by CMTEDD to send you information and updates about new opportunities to have your say. You can unsubscribe from these updates notifications at any time. If you subscribe to receive updates about a specific engagement project, for example by using the ‘Follow’ function, the email address you provide will be used to send you information and updates about that engagement. You can unsubscribe from these notifications at any time. Cookies Cookies are used on our site, but they do not collect any personal information . For the most part they are sessional and just contain system-generated values to identify the user's session for statistical and system administration purposes only. For more information on Cookies and Google Analytics, please refer to the CMTEDD Privacy Policy . Site visit data The site’s web-server automatically collects the following de-identified data for statistical and system administration purposes only: your server (or IP) address the day and time you visited the site the pages you visited on our site the address of the last page you visited the operating system you are using rough geographic location (down to the city) language (e.g. American English) internet service provider (e.g. Telstra) the type of browser and version you are using. To the extent that this data could make you identifiable, CMTEDD and Social Pinpoint will not attempt to identify individuals from the records the server automatically generates unless necessary to investigate a breach of law or regulation. Who has access to information that is collected from you? When you sign up for and use the ‘YourSay’ service you provide two types of information: information that is publicly available; and information that is available to CMTEDD and Social Pinpoint in its capacity as CMTEDD’s contracted service provider (and its agents and sub-contractors who may be based overseas, namely, in the Philippines) and which may be made available by CMTEDD to other entities as set out in this privacy notice. Publicly available information Publicly available information is limited to your username and any comments you leave under that username in the forums or other feedback tools published to ‘YourSay’. You can use your first name or an anonymous username if you do not want your full name attached to forum and guestbook comments, stories or questions. Feedback (including overall results of polls and surveys, and in some instances, quotes from forums and surveys) may be published in publicly available reports at the end of the consultation period. Please note that the ACT Government is subject to the Freedom of Information Act 2016 . The Freedom of Information Act 2016 provides a general right of access to government information. This includes documents created by the government, documents held by contracted service providers relating to the performance of government contracts and documents supplied to government by external organisations or individuals. Information available to CMTEDD and Social Pinpoint (and which CMTEDD may disclose to other entities as set out in this privacy notice) includes : all information from the sign-up form comments, questions, stories, guestbook posts survey responses, quick poll responses, map pins general site activity such as document downloads, videos viewed, images viewed information on the technology used to access the site. Information available to third party contractors may include but is not limited to : comments, questions, stories, guestbook posts survey responses, quick poll responses, map pins de-identified data for reporting purposes. Disclosure of personal information CMTEDD will take all reasonable measures to prevent unauthorised access to, or disclosure of, your personal information . Organisations to which personal information is disclosed include other ACT Government directorates, the ACT Government’s contracted Service Providers, such as Social Pinpoint and their subcontractors or agents who may be based in Australia or overseas (namely in the Philippines), who perform various services for and on behalf of the ACT Government. These contractors have agreed to be bound by the provisions of the Information Privacy Act 2014 . We will also take all necessary measures to ensure that your personal information is not disclosed to other individuals, institutions and authorities except in accordance with the Information Privacy Act 2014 , such as if required or authorised by law or explicitly permitted by you. Some examples of when information may be provided to another person without your consent include in the event of an investigation into suspected unlawful or improper activity or when a law enforcement agency or government agency may exercise its legal authority to inspect the web server's records (e.g. in relation to hacking or abusive messages). Access and correction You may seek corrections to your personal information that CMTEDD has collected if you believe it is inaccurate, out-of–date, incomplete, irrelevant or misleading. CMTEDD is required to take reasonable steps to correct personal information to ensure that, having regard to the purpose for which it is held, the information is not inaccurate, out-of–date, incomplete, irrelevant or misleading. You may also seek access to your personal information that CMTEDD holds. More information about seeking access to, and correction of, your personal information held by CMTEDD can be found in the CMTEDD Information Privacy Policy . Links The ‘YourSay’ Privacy Statement does not apply to third party websites or digital services which may be linked to from content published to 'YourSay'. We recommend you read the privacy statement of the relevant service when you access these sites. Third Party Providers We sometimes use third party providers for some web-based services, with information stored in the United States and Europe. These include Campaign Monitor and Mail Chimp for email subscriptions, Survey Monkey and Typeform for online surveys, Social Pinpoint for interactive maps, Viostream for live streaming question and answers, MindHive for running a collaborative forum and EventBrite for registration at events. Please follow the hyperlinks for details on their privacy policies. Campaign Monitor Privacy CMTEDD uses Campaign Monitor to provide electronic newsletters to subscribers. In distributing newsletters, CMTEDD, via Campaign Monitor, will collect personal information from you, including email addresses you have provided to CMTEDD for the purpose of receiving electronic newsletters, all information relating to those email addresses, and in some cases your name. Campaign Monitor also uses cookies, web beacons and Flash player codes to collect information for use by CMTEDD about: when you access CMTEDD or other ACT Government electronic newsletters your browser type and version your operating system and other similar information your IP address and its geolocation clicks on email links and whether the email is forwarded. CMTEDD holds the Campaign Monitor account and personal information collected through that account can be accessed by other agencies of the ACT Government for the purposes of sending electronic newsletters. For additional detail about the information Campaign Monitor will collect, please refer to Campaign Monitor’s Privacy Policy and Campaign Monitor’s Terms of Use . Campaign Monitor will use the information collected from you for the purpose of providing the online service which enables CMTEDD and other agencies of the ACT Government to create, send and manage electronic newsletters. Campaign Monitor will also use this information to measure the performance of CMTEDD and other ACT Government email campaigns. Campaign Monitor may transfer this information to its contractors or other third parties who process the information on Campaign Monitor’s behalf, or where otherwise required to do so by law. Campaign Monitor is based in the United States of America (USA) and is subject to the laws of the USA. Your information (including your IP address) will be transmitted to and stored by Campaign Monitor on servers located outside Australia. You can unsubscribe from the 'YourSay' electronic newsletter at any time by selecting the 'unsubscribe’ option in every email sent to you by Campaign Monitor. More information about how CMTEDD manages the personal information it collects can be found at https://www.act.gov.au/directorates-and-agencies/chief-minister-treasury-and-economic-development-directorate/cmtedd-privacy . If you have any questions relating to the use of your personal data please contact askus@yoursay.act.gov.au . Information in the CRM may be used to inform subsequent engagements with the same or similar stakeholders. The use of the database is intended to strengthen coordination between ACT Public Sector agencies and reduce duplication of effort and stakeholder fatigue, by sharing information about engagement activities across government. records.resolved_title: Safer overtaking and stronger flood resilience for the Bruce at Goorganga
records.body_text: Safer overtaking and stronger flood resilience for the Bruce at Goorganga - Ministerial Media Statements search menu Search Queensland Government The Queensland Cabinet and Ministerial Directory Published Today at 10:00 AM Minister for Transport and Main Roads The Honourable Brent Mickelberg Safer overtaking and stronger flood resilience for the Bruce at Goorganga Construction has now commenced on new overtaking lanes at Goorganga while design progresses for future flood resilience upgrades. The works will improve safety, freight efficiency and network resilience on a key section of the Bruce Highway, helping get Queenslanders home sooner and safer. The project is jointly funded, demonstrating the Albanese and Crisafulli Governments’ commitment to fixing the Bruce and strengthening regional Queensland connections. The upgrades will deliver safer and more reliable journeys for North Queensland communities during severe weather events. The Albanese and Crisafulli Governments are progressing another milestone for fixing the Bruce, with construction now underway on new overtaking lanes at Goorganga Plains, south of Proserpine. The project will deliver new northbound and southbound overtaking lanes on the Bruce Highway, improving safety, reducing driver frustration and supporting more efficient journeys for freight operators, tourists and local communities. The upgrade will also include roadside safety improvements and upgrades to the Gunyarra Road intersection, including improved lighting and pavement treatments. Importantly, design work is also progressing on future flood immunity upgrades along this section of the Bruce Highway, helping ensure a safer and more resilient connection for North Queensland communities during major weather events. The proposed flood resilience improvements would raise 10.6 kilometres of highway between Thompson Creek and Lethebrook, improve drainage infrastructure and deliver new bridges and intersection upgrades designed to keep the highway open for longer during severe weather. The works are being delivered as part of a jointly funded Bruce Highway investment to boost safety for the spine of the State, getting Queenslanders home sooner and safer. Federal Minister for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government Catherine King said the project would deliver important benefits for motorists and freight operators travelling between Mackay and Proserpine. "The Albanese Government is investing in projects that improve safety, reliability and resilience on the Bruce Highway," Minister King said. "These upgrades will help create a safer and more reliable route for local communities, freight operators and visitors while supporting long-term economic growth across North Queensland." Queensland Minister for Transport and Main Roads Brent Mickelberg said the project was another important milestone in the Crisafulli Government's commitment to fixing the Bruce. "The Bruce Highway is the backbone of Queensland and we're getting on with the job of delivering the upgrades needed get Queenslanders home safer and sooner," Minister Mickelberg said. "These overtaking lanes will provide safer opportunities for motorists to pass slower-moving vehicles, improve freight efficiency and deliver smoother journeys on a critical section of the highway. “These works will improve journeys for commuters now, while laying the groundwork for a more resilient Bruce Highway. Major flood resilience upgrades are already being designed to help keep North Queensland communities connected during severe weather.” Member for Whitsunday Amanda Camm said the project would provide lasting benefits for local communities and industries. "Anyone who regularly drives this section of the Bruce Highway understands how important these upgrades are for safety and reliability," Ms Camm said. "This investment will improve travel conditions for local residents, tourists and freight operators while supporting the industries and businesses that keep our region moving. "Locals have endured the impacts of flooding in this region, so it is fantastic to also see planning underway to deliver infrastructure improvements to improve flood resilience where it is needed most.” ENDS MEDIA CONTACTS : Minister King: Jack Begbie, 0481 759 580 Minister Mickelberg: Mardi Norton, 0467 746 523

records.body_text: Contractor appointed to deliver 600-bed Coomera Hospital - Ministerial Media Statements search menu Search Queensland Government The Queensland Cabinet and Ministerial Directory Published Today at 11:53 AM JOINT STATEMENT Premier and Minister for Veterans The Honourable David Crisafulli Minister for Health and Ambulance Services The Honourable Tim Nicholls Contractor appointed to deliver 600-bed Coomera Hospital The Coomera Hospital is one step closer with the appointment of a major contractor to deliver the project meaning construction activity will now accelerate, including civil works, retaining walls and permanent stormwater management. Works on the multi-storey car park are expected to start next month. The Crisafulli Government’s fully-funded Hospital Rescue Plan will deliver 600 beds at the new Coomera Hospital, 200 more than planned under the former Government. The Crisafulli Government is delivering health services when Queenslanders need them and healing Labor’s Health Crisis. The Crisafulli Government has appointed Multiplex to deliver the new 600-bed Coomera Hospital, marking a major milestone in providing more hospital capacity for the rapidly growing northern Gold Coast. It follows major foundation works which are already underway, including concrete pours to support the expanded footprint, adding to retaining and remodelling of existing structures, as well as bulk earth works. The Crisafulli Government is delivering health services when Queenslanders need them, with several stages of the new Coomera Hospital to be delivered from 2028, starting with the car park through to all 600 beds by 2032. An independent review of the project found the new hospital had been under-scoped and underfunded by the former Government, with the unbudgeted 400-bed plan failing to meet the future needs of one of the State’s fastest-growing communities. Under the Crisafulli Government’s Hospital Rescue Plan , the project was rescoped, with 200 additional hospital beds added, delivering the capacity needed for the Northern Gold Coast with a new 600-bed hospital. Multiplex will deliver the major infrastructure project, with civil works, construction of retaining walls, permanent stormwater management tanks and works on the multi-storey car park expected to start from next month. Major foundation works are already underway, including concrete pours to support the expanded footprint, alongside retaining works, remodelling of existing structures and bulk eart works. The new Coomera Hospital is part of the Crisafulli Government’s fully-funded Hospital Rescue Plan , delivering more than 2,600 additional beds, three new hospitals and major expansions at 10 hospitals across Queensland. On the Gold Coast, 110 new hospital beds have already been delivered at Gold Coast University Hospital under the Hospital Rescue Plan , with 828 additional frontline health workers added since the Crisafulli Government was elected. More health workers and hospital beds have delivered the lowest quarterly ambulance ramping rates recorded in a decade, with 20.1% at the Gold Coast University Hospital and 11.6% at Robina Hospital. Premier David Crisafulli said the 600-bed Coomera Hospital would deliver health services when Queenslanders need them for the rapidly growing northern Gold Coast. “The northern Gold Coast is one of the fastest-growing parts of Queensland, and we’re making sure families have access to health services when they need them, as their communities continue to grow,” Premier Crisafulli said. “We’re delivering a bigger, better Coomera Hospital, with 200 more beds because Queenslanders deserve easier access to health services and health infrastructure that keeps pace with population growth.” Minister for Health and Ambulance Services Tim Nicholls said the Crisafulli Government was building the beds, growing the workforce and improving patient flow to heal Labor’s Health Crisis. “Labor had a decade to plan for the growth of the northern Gold Coast but left behind an underfunded and under-scoped 400-bed proposal that could never have been delivered as promised,” Minister Nicholls said. “We made the choice to fix the project, add 200 beds, and properly plan and fund the hospital this community needs, and we’re now getting on with delivering it.” Member for Coomera Michael Crandon said the community was now seeing real progress on the hospital construction. “Foundations are underway and major construction activity is ramping up on site, giving families across the Northern Gold Coast confidence their new hospital is moving ahead,” Mr Crandon said. Member for Theodore Mark Boothman said the new hospital would strengthen health services across the northern Gold Coast. “This 600-bed hospital will mean more care closer to home for local families, while adding much-needed capacity across the Gold Coast health system,” Mr Boothman said. ENDS MEDIA CONTACT: Emma Morton, 0410 657 890

records.resolved_title: PISA proves Australian teachers are world-class but need more support
records.body_text: PISA proves Australian teachers are world-class but need more support | Australian Greens Skip to main content Search Search PISA proves Australian teachers are world-class but need more support 2026-09-09 The Greens say the national conversation around classroom disruption and student performance is broken, with the latest PISA data showing Australian teachers are among the most attentive and hardest-working in the world. According to PISA data about learning conditions in Australian science classes: 79% of students say their teacher shows an interest in every student’s learning, compared with 69% across the OECD 80% say their teacher gives extra help when students need it, compared with the 73% OECD average 73% say their teacher continues teaching until students understand, compared with 66% for the OECD The Greens say the results should prompt a much deeper discussion about student disengagement, teacher shortages, school funding, inequality and whether the Australian model of education is capable of meeting the needs of every young person. Comments attributable to Senator Penny Allman-Payne, Australian Greens Spokesperson for Primary and Secondary Education: “Blaming teachers and kids is not going to end classroom disruption. “Kids aren’t acting up for the hell of it. They’re disruptive because they’re disengaged, and they’re disengaged because teachers aren’t empowered and supported to ensure learning works for every student. “We need to fully fund our public schools, giving our overworked and overstretched teachers the resources and support they need to provide the education our kids deserve. “We also need to have a serious conversation about Australia’s one-size-fits-all approach to education and the way particular pedagogies are being forced down teacher’s throats, undermining their skills and experience and ensuring our kids keep falling further behind.”

records.body_text: Avoca Drive upgrade powering ahead with shovels to hit the ground 18 months ahead of schedule | NSW Government menu Open Menu MyServiceNSW Logged in MyServiceNSW Manage account Logout of MyServiceNSW Ministerial media release Avoca Drive upgrade powering ahead with shovels to hit the ground 18 months ahead of schedule Published: 9 September 2026 Released by: The Premier, Minister for the Central Coast, Minister for Roads Listen Shovels will hit the ground 18 months ahead of schedule on Stage One of the Avoca Drive Upgrade, with the project given the green light to start works before the end of the year. The project is backed by a $100 million investment from the Albanese Labor Government and $30 million from the Minns Labor Government. The major upgrade will tackle one of the Central Coast’s biggest congestion bottlenecks, delivering two lanes in each direction, intersection upgrades and better connections for pedestrians, cyclists and public transport users. A key east-west route on the Central Coast, Avoca Drive carries around 26,000 vehicles a day and provides access to Kincumber Village Shopping Centre, local schools, sporting facilities, businesses and community services. Works on Stage One will start before the end of the year, with construction ramping up in early 2027. The project will widen 1km of Avoca Drive to two lanes in each direction between the Bungoona Road and Carrak Road, and Joalah Road and Killuna Road intersections, upgrade three intersections, deliver new pedestrian crossings, and improve active and public transport connections. A new roundabout at Bungoona Road and Kincumber Street will improve access to the Kincumber Village Shopping Centre. Earlier this year, the community provided feedback on the proposal which was considered and addressed in the Determination Report and is now available on the project webpage . Just months after the community was invited to have its say, the project has cleared the approval process and is moving into construction, with the NSW Government’s Project Swift initiative accelerating delivery by progressing planning, design and procurement activities in tandem and streamlining key processes – bringing construction forward by more than 18 months. Work is already progressing behind the scenes to prepare for construction, with GHD Pty Ltd engaged to develop detailed design and procurement for a construction contractor well underway. The Minns Labor Government will also undertake planning for the upgrade of Avoca Drive, west of Kincumber. Quotes attributable to Premier of New South Wales, Chris Minns: “Avoca Drive is a critical link used by thousands of Central Coast drivers every day. Across the Central Coast Local Health District, the proportion of triage category 2 patients – people with life threatening conditions – being treated on time improved in the April to June 2026 quarter to 72 per cent compared to four years ago (55.7 per cent in 2022 under the Liberals). The Minns Labor Government’s 2026-27 Budget also delivered a record boost of $10.3 billion to help recruit an additional 9,000 health workers, deliver record pay rises for nurses and midwives, and expand services, as well as $11.9 billion to deliver 32 new and upgraded hospitals and more than 2,500 additional beds and treatment spaces across the state. These are beds that cannot be used by patients needing hospital care. “Each of these beds represents an individual who cannot be given certainty about their future. For older and vulnerable patients, these extended stays have real impacts on mobility and wellbeing. These 86 patients deserve more than unknown wait times. “Despite this, I am pleased to see progress being made across emergency department wait times as a result of investment by the Minns Labor Government. I will continue to work with my Central Coast Labor colleagues to make sure that our community always has access to the care they need, when they need it most.” Quotes attributable to Member for the Entrance David Mehan: “The number of people stuck in hospital waiting for Commonwealth aged care and NDIS support is disheartening, but I am pleased to see patients across the Central Coast are seeing better results in our emergency departments. “More people with serious conditions are being treated on time at Gosford and Wyong, while fewer people are presenting with less urgent conditions. “This is a credit to our hardworking health staff and the investment by the Minns Labor Government in more staff, beds and services like Long Jetty Urgent Care Service. “There’s more to do, but these results show we’re heading in the right direction.” Related ministerial articles Ministerial media release Commonwealth stranded patients put pressure on Northern NSW hospitals As of 30 June 2026, there were 63 stranded patients waiting for Commonwealth aged care and NDIS placements in hospitals across Northern NSW. The new accommodation, which will help attract and retain more frontline healthcare workers to the region, includes eight single bed and two double bed self-contained units, located on the Wyong Hospital campus. The designs show each unit with kitchen, living areas and ensuite bathrooms. One of the single bed units is also designed to be fully wheelchair accessible with all functional areas designed to accommodate wheelchair occupants. Construction is expected to begin in February 2027 following a tender process to award a building contractor to deliver the works. Wyong is one of more than 20 Key Health Worker Accommodation projects in rural, regional and remote NSW, as part of the Minns Labor Government’s $200.1 million program. The funding includes the building of new accommodation, refurbishment of existing living quarters, and the purchase of suitable properties such as residential units. This investment builds on the $45.3 million in accommodation for key healthcare workers in the Murrumbidgee, Southern NSW, and Far West Local Health Districts, which is now complete with all new accommodation delivered and fully operational. The $200.1 million Key Health Worker Accommodation is one of several initiatives the NSW Government is using to strengthen the regional health workforce. Other initiatives include: The NSW Rural Health Workforce Incentive Scheme, which provides incentives of up to $20,000 for the hardest to fill and critically vacant positions in rural and regional NSW. Expanded training pathways, such as the Rural Generalist Single Employer Pathway, which has assisted 74 doctors to train as rural generalists across NSW. Investing $83 million to boost maternity care across regional NSW, including funding for an additional 53 full-time equivalent midwives. Delivering study subsidies for regional health workers. Delivering an extra 500 regional paramedics. The opening of the M1 Pacific Motorway extension marks a major milestone for the Hunter, closing a missing link in the Sydney to Brisbane economic corridor and strengthening one of Australia’s most important freight routes. The M1 Pacific Motorway extension and Hexham Straight widening projects were jointly funded with a total investment of $2.24 billion – $1.79 billion from the Albanese Government and $448 million from the Minns Government. It builds on Labor’s long record of investment in transforming the Pacific Highway. Between 2007 and 2013, the former Federal Labor Government committed more than $8.7 billion to complete the duplication of the Pacific Highway and deliver bypasses of towns across New South Wales. Since coming to government in 2022, the Albanese Government has committed a further $266.4 million to finish the remaining upgrades along the corridor, in addition to its investment in the M1 extension. The new motorway will provide a direct connection between the M1 at Black Hill and Raymond Terrace, improving connections to jobs, businesses, communities and major regional infrastructure, including Newcastle Airport and the Port of Newcastle. For motorists, it means cutting travel times by seven to nine minutes during peak hours and removing up to 25,000 vehicles a day from local streets. For freight, it means a faster and more reliable connection through the Hunter and along the Sydney to Brisbane corridor. The project has also been a major investment in local jobs and skills, with 70 per cent of the workforce drawn from the Hunter region and 99 apprentices and trainees gaining experience on the project. More than 2,700 workers have helped deliver the extension, clocking up more than four million hours of work to get the motorway open around 18 months earlier than originally planned. Construction of the motorway has been delivered on a remarkable scale, including: * More than 1.6 million cubic metres of earth moved – enough to fill around 650 Olympic-sized swimming pools More than 720,000 tonnes of rock imported and placed across the project Construction of 11 bridges, supported by 278 bridge piles and 863 bridge girders More than 520 kilometres of drainage and wick drains installed 96 per cent of construction waste diverted from landfill 435 habitat structures installed to support native wildlife After years of planning and construction, the M1 extension is now ready to become part of everyday life across the Hunter – delivering a new connection that will transform the movement of people and freight and support the region’s next era of growth. A road that will support families, workers, local businesses and our industries. “I am incredibly proud to see this mammoth investment into the Hunter be days from opening. “This is Labor delivering for the Hunter.” Quotes attributable to Federal Member for Paterson, Meryl Swanson: “Today is a really proud day for our community. "Not only are we delivering the M1 Extension to Raymond Terrace, we're opening it more than a year ahead of schedule - funded, fast-tracked and delivered. That's what happens when governments work together, back our region and get on with the job. "This project belongs to the thousands of local workers who helped make it happen. From the engineers and planners to the crews on the ground, thank you. As I always say, Hunter workers work harder, and this road is proof of that.” Quotes attributable to Federal Member for Newcastle, Sharon Claydon: “This completed link secures Newcastle as the economic centre of the Hunter by keeping freight as well as general traffic moving safer and smoother in all directions for years to come. “After providing a massive boost to local jobs with more than four million hours of construction, the finished motorway now becomes a permanent and reliable pathway for industrial growth across the Hunter.” Quotes attributable to State Member for Port Stephens, Kate Washington: “Woohoo! records.body_text: Major milestone reached for Lismore Build to Rent homes | NSW Government menu Open Menu MyServiceNSW Logged in MyServiceNSW Manage account Logout of MyServiceNSW Ministerial media release Major milestone reached for Lismore Build to Rent homes Published: 9 September 2026 Released by: Minister for Planning and Public Spaces, Minister for Recovery Listen Residents are one step closer to moving into affordable, long-term housing, with Landcom reaching a major milestone by completing the topping out of its Build-to-Rent project in East Lismore. Work to complete the project has progressed rapidly, bringing 50 new Build-to-Rent apartments closer to completion. Major construction works are set to finish by late 2026, with the finished touches expected to be finished in early 2027, weather permitting. The Crawford and Military Road site is a first-of-its-kind project for Lismore, delivered by the NSW Government’s developer, Landcom. Key highlights of the project include: Affordable Housing : 20% of the homes are reserved as affordable rental housing for residents on low-to-moderate incomes. Flood-Resilient Living : Built safely above the flood zone to offer long-term stability and security for residents. Diverse Housing Mix : A selection of studio, 1, 2, and 3-bedroom apartments designed to suit a variety of household needs. Prime Location : Situated close to local shops, schools, Southern Cross University, and parklands. Landcom will retain ownership of the properties, with a dedicated operator to be appointed by the end of the year to manage the homes. The site sits next to the NSW Reconstruction Authority land at Crawford Road, which will also be redeveloped by Landcom to deliver more than 500 additional new homes for the East Lismore community. Landcom continues to deliver thousands of homes across NSW through its portfolio of projects in Greater Sydney and regional communities including the Northern Rivers, South Coast and Central West. The Minns Labor Government's planning reforms and surplus land audit have grown the pipeline of homes for NSW, with the highest number of homes under construction in the country; more than 80,000 homes, and more in the development pipeline. For more information on the East Lismore project go to: www.landcom.com.au/eastlismore Minister for Planning and Public Spaces Paul Scully said: "This is an important milestone for Lismore and means we’re just around the corner from seeing renters move into their new homes. Minister for Recovery, Minister for the North Coast and Member for Lismore Janelle Saffin said: "Long-term security remain critical challenges for Lismore as we continue our rebuild. Reaching this milestone brings 50 beautifully designed, flood free apartments another step closer for our community. records.body_text: Minns Government delivers $350,000 boost for Rehab In The Home in southern Lake Macquarie | NSW Government menu Open Menu MyServiceNSW Logged in MyServiceNSW Manage account Logout of MyServiceNSW Ministerial media release Minns Government delivers $350,000 boost for Rehab In The Home in southern Lake Macquarie Published: 7 September 2026 Released by: Minister for Health, Minister for Regional Health Listen The Minns Government is investing $350,000 to expand Rehab In The Home services across southern Lake Macquarie, helping more people access rehabilitation and recovery services closer to home. Rehab In The Home enables eligible patients to receive rehabilitation care in their own homes, supporting recovery while reducing the need to travel for appointments. Funded as part of the 2026-27 State Budget, the investment will support allied health professionals from Hunter New England Local Health District to deliver the expanded community-based services to the southern Lake Macquarie region. The services will include community orthopaedic rehabilitation as well as discharge supports for patients returning home from Central Coast hospitals. The expansion builds on the successful rollout of nurse practitioner-led wound care, continence and aged care outreach clinics in early 2025, which have experienced increasing demand. As one of the fastest-growing areas in the region, southern Lake Macquarie continues to see increasing demand for local health services. The expanded outreach and rehabilitation services will make it easier for older people, people living with disability or mobility challenges, and families to access the care they need closer to home. This investment reflects the NSW Government's commitment to ensuring people living in growing communities can access high-quality healthcare services when and where they need them. This year the Minns Government delivered a $10.3 billion boost to health services across NSW as part of the 26-27 Budget, the largest increase to the health budget in the state’s history. As the population gets older and health systems around the world experience significant pressure, this record investment ensures a more sustainable future for NSW healthcare. Quotes attributable to Minister for Health and Minister for Regional Health Ryan Park: “Southern Lake Macquarie is one of the fastest growing areas in the region, and our local health services need to keep pace with that growth. “We know travel can create a barrier for people with mobility challenges, Rehab in The Home can make a considerable difference to their comfort, independence and dignity during recovery. “Expanding the service allows more people to recover safely in their own homes, meaning less disruptions, better continuity of care and reduced physical and psychological strain.“ Quotes attributable to the Member for Swansea, Yasmin Catley: “As a local, I know how important it is for people here to be able to access the care that’s close to home and loved ones. “This service will mean people can get that support closer to home, surrounded by their family, friends and community and that matters when you’re recovering. “This is about giving people the best possible chance to recover, rebuild their independence and get back to living their lives close to where their lives already are.” Quotes attributable to Member for Lake Macquarie Greg Piper: “People in southern Lake Macquarie have told us they want access to more services closer to home, and this investment is a direct response to that need. “This additional funding will support the earlier discharge of patients from hospitals and strengthen local rehabilitation services, making it easier for residents to get the support they need in their own homes and community”. Quotes attributable to Tracey McCosker PSM, Chief Executive, Hunter New England Local Health District “Providing care closer to home improves the experience of patients and their families, while helping people stay connected to the support networks that are so important to recovery. “This investment will enable our District to expand services in southern Lake Macquarie and ensure more people can access high-quality rehabilitation and recovery support in their local community.” Related ministerial articles Ministerial media release First major concrete pour for Tamworth’s Nioka Palliative Care Unit expansion The expansion of the Nioka Palliative Care Unit at Tamworth Hospital has reached an important milestone, with the first major concrete pour completed for the new building.
