records.body_text: New Wyong Hospital Palliative Care Unit officially open | NSW Government menu Open Menu MyServiceNSW Logged in MyServiceNSW Manage account Logout of MyServiceNSW Ministerial media release New Wyong Hospital Palliative Care Unit officially open Published: 7 September 2026 Released by: Minister for the Central Coast, Minister for Regional Health Listen The official opening of the new Palliative Care Unit at Wyong Hospital will be held today, marking an important milestone in the delivery of high-quality end-of-life care for the Central Coast community. Delivered as part of the Minns Labor Government’s $93 million capital investment in the World Class End of Life Care program, the new unit has been designed to provide privacy, comfort and dignity for people in the final stages of life, providing the highest standard of care and support close to home. The purpose-built unit is located in an existing building at the eastern end of the Wyong Hospital and features 12 palliative care bedrooms with ensuites, communal areas, meeting spaces and flexible outdoor spaces. Developed in close consultation with local community members and palliative care staff, the facility has been tailored to meet the needs of patients, families, loved ones and the broader Central Coast community. Local community group, The Elsie’s Palliative Care Project, has made a generous contribution to the new unit, providing family and overnight room furnishings, specialist beds, garden enhancements and a range of additional amenities to help provide additional comfort and support for patients, families and carers. Key design elements include: Spacious bedrooms to accommodate visiting family members, featuring home-like interior finishes and large windows overlooking private gardens Individual patient balconies, enabling patients to move outdoors on their bed to enjoy the garden A large family room with dining spaces where family and visitors can gather and share meals. A landscaped garden, with existing mature trees retained to provide a natural outlook from patient bedrooms. A communal outdoor area that provides a private and reflective space. An overnight room to allow additional family members to stay close to their family. The Wyong Palliative Care Unit was delivered by Health Infrastructure in partnership with Central Coast Local Health District and builder, Renascent Australia. The $93 million World Class End of Life Care program is delivering new and redeveloped palliative care facilities across the state. Other locations include Nepean, Westmead, Tamworth and Orange hospitals. For more information about the World Class End of Life Program, visit hinfra.health.nsw.gov.au/projects/project-search/end-of-life-care-program Quotes attributable to Minister for Regional Health Ryan Park: “The Minns Government is committed to ensuring people with life-limiting illnesses receive high quality end-of-life care at the right time, and in the right place. “This modern and purpose-built Palliative Care Unit at Wyong will provide comfort, dignity and compassionate care in what can be a very difficult time for patients and their families.” Quotes attributable to Minister for the Central Coast and Member for Wyong David Harris: “This new unit is a wonderful facility for the Wyong community and a great addition our region’s existing palliative care services, including the palliative care unit at Gosford Hospital and in-home services to meet individual and family needs. “People have different needs and preferences when it comes to end-of-life care. This new unit will give patients and their families access to that care close to home. “It’s an important investment in palliative care on the Central Coast and will provide patients and families with greater choice and support when they need it most.” Quotes attributable to Member for Gosford Liesl Tesch: “This milestone opening is so important to ensure that every family can access end-of-life in the utmost comfort and dignity. “In the heartbreaking reality of end-of-life care, this unit meets the unique needs of palliative care while ensuring that no one in our community has to travel far from home to find comfort, dignity and support in their final days.” Quotes attributable to Central Coast Local Health District Acting Chief Executive Jude Constable: "The opening of this purpose-built unit is an important milestone for palliative care on the Central Coast. “This will provide another care option alongside our established services at Gosford Hospital and in the community, ensuring people can receive the support that best meets their needs. records.body_text: Next Stage of Hume Highway Upgrade at Table Top to start | NSW Government menu Open Menu MyServiceNSW Logged in MyServiceNSW Manage account Logout of MyServiceNSW Ministerial media release Next Stage of Hume Highway Upgrade at Table Top to start Published: 9 September 2026 Released by: Minister for Regional NSW Listen The Minns Labor Government is continuing work to improve one of Australia’s busiest freight and transport corridors, with the next stage of a major upgrade to the Hume Highway at Table Top to begin later this month. Transport for NSW is upgrading a 3.3 kilometre section of the northbound lanes and a 3.15 kilometre section of the southbound lanes, delivering a smoother, safer and more durable road surface while reducing the need for ongoing maintenance. Work includes road reconstruction and resurfacing, drainage improvements, new safety barriers, updated signs and line marking. The first stage of the project, covering the southern 1.65 kilometres of the northbound lanes and upgrades to two crossovers, was completed in June 2026. The next stage will upgrade the remaining 1.65 kilometres of the northbound lanes, with work planned to start on Friday 18 September and take around 12 weeks to complete, weather permitting. Stage three, covering the southbound lanes, will be carried out next financial year. During stage two, the Tynan Road intersection with the Hume Highway will close from Friday 25 September, with changed traffic conditions also in place at the Burma Road intersection. Traffic controls and temporary safety measures will be in place throughout the work to safely manage vehicles through the area and minimise risks while crews are working near the intersections. Motorists will use the same detours and traffic arrangements that were successfully implemented during the first stage of work. At least one lane will remain open in each direction during construction. Motorists should expect lane closures, contraflow arrangements on the southbound lanes and reduced speed limits through the work zone. Most work will be carried out Monday to Friday between 6am and 11pm, and on Saturdays between 7am and 5pm. Minister for Regional NSW and Duty MLC for the Electorate of Albury, Tara Moriarty said: “The Minns Labor Government is investing in the roads regional communities, businesses and freight operators rely on every day. “The Hume Highway is a vital link between regional NSW, Sydney and Melbourne, carrying thousands of motorists and freight vehicles every day. “This upgrade will make the journey safer, smoother and more reliable, while delivering a stronger road surface that can better withstand the heavy freight that uses this important corridor. “Strong regional economies need strong transport connections. This investment will help businesses move goods, support local jobs and keep communities connected. “We’ve already delivered the first stage of this upgrade, and this next package of work will build on that progress. “We thank motorists and the local community for their patience while this work is underway. Please follow changed traffic conditions, take care around work sites and allow extra time for your journey.” Related ministerial articles Ministerial media release Avoca Drive upgrade powering ahead with shovels to hit the ground 18 months ahead of schedule Shovels will hit the ground 18 months ahead of schedule on Stage One of the Avoca Drive Upgrade, with the project given the green light to start works before the end of the year. records.body_text: Design released for long-awaited Spring Farm Parkway extension | NSW Government menu Open Menu MyServiceNSW Logged in MyServiceNSW Manage account Logout of MyServiceNSW Ministerial media release Design released for long-awaited Spring Farm Parkway extension Published: 7 September 2026 Released by: Deputy Premier, Minister for Roads, Minister for Western Sydney Listen The Minns and Albanese Labor Governments are today unveiling the proposed design for Spring Farm Parkway Stage 2, a three-kilometre, four-lane road that would complete the east-west link between Menangle Park and Spring Farm. The community are now able to have their say on the proposed design and Review of Environmental Factors (REF) for the project, which is in response to longstanding calls from the local community for a direct connection between the Camden area and the Hume Motorway. Currently, Spring Farm Parkway has no direct road connection through to the suburb of Spring Farm – as originally intended. This has meant motorists are forced to travel via Narellan Road, adding unnecessary time and distance to their journeys and putting additional pressure on this key road corridor as Camden continues to grow. The former New South Wales Liberal-National Government split the project in two and progressed only Stage 1 of the project, which opened to traffic in August 2024, but failed to fund or progress Stage 2 – leaving the critical connection through to Spring Farm unfinished. Stage 2 would complete the final section of the corridor, allowing motorists to drive on a continuous east-west connection from Menangle Road and the Hume Motorway through Spring Farm to the Camden Bypass. The Albanese and Minns Labor Governments have committed $15 million to progress the planning for Stage 2. The public can now view the proposed plan and provide feedback to inform the final design. Delivery funding would be considered through future Budget processes following the completion of planning and design work. For further information and submitting feedback https://www.transport.nsw.gov.au/projects/current-projects/spring-farm-parkway-stage-2 Federal Minister for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government, Catherine King said: “The Albanese Government is working in partnership with the Minns Government to provide funding for infrastructure that keeps pace with the growth of Sydney’s southwest. “By progressing the planning of Spring Farm Parkway Stage 2, we are taking an important step towards ensuring that families in Menangle Park and Spring Farm have the safe, reliable and efficient road link to the Hume Highway that they deserve.” NSW Deputy Premier and Minister for Western Sydney, Prue Car said: "Southwest Sydney has waited long enough for the roads it was promised. The second stage of Spring Farm Parkway will finish a job that was abandoned by the former Liberal National government halfway through. This will ensure the growing Macarthur region finally gets the connection it needs.” NSW Minister for Roads, Jenny Aitchison said: “The former Liberal-National Government built half a road and called it done, leaving a community with a road that leads to nowhere and putting more pressure on the surrounding road network. “Like the local community, we want to see Spring Farm Parkway do what it was intended to do – connect through to Spring Farm. “This is an important step forward, and I encourage locals to have their say on the proposed design. records.body_text: Stranded aged care and NDIS patients predicted to reach 1,700 in 2027 | NSW Government menu Open Menu MyServiceNSW Logged in MyServiceNSW Manage account Logout of MyServiceNSW Ministerial media release Stranded aged care and NDIS patients predicted to reach 1,700 in 2027 Published: 9 September 2026 Released by: Minister for Health Listen NSW emergency departments are treating more patients on time and ambulances are getting back on the road faster, despite growing pressure from patients who are medically ready to leave hospital but are waiting for aged care or NDIS support. The latest Bureau of Health Information quarterly data shows 68.7 per cent of patients were treated on time in the April to June quarter, up from 62.8 per cent four years ago, while timely transfers from ambulances to emergency departments improved from 72.5 per cent to 80.3 per cent over the same period. But those improvements are being made against a growing challenge inside NSW hospitals: more than 1,300 patients who no longer need hospital treatment cannot leave because they are waiting for Commonwealth funded aged care or NDIS support. That number increased by almost 300 in the past year and NSW Health estimates it could reach almost 1,700 by June 2027 if current trends continue. For patients, that can mean spending weeks or months in hospital when they would be better cared for at home, in aged care or appropriate disability accommodation. For hospitals, it means fewer beds available for people coming through emergency departments who need them. The scale of the challenge means the equivalent of one in every eight beds accessible from NSW emergency departments is currently occupied by someone who is medically ready to leave hospital but cannot – up from around one in ten a year ago. Older people waiting for aged care account for much of the increase, rising almost 40 per cent in a year from 761 to 1,063 patients. Bed block growing across Sydney The impact of Commonwealth aged care and NDIS delays is being felt in some of Sydney's busiest hospitals. The number of patients waiting for aged care or NDIS support in South Eastern Sydney increased from 68 to 157 in the year to June 2026. At St George Hospital, the number increased from 17 to 64 – the largest increase and highest number of any hospital in NSW – while Prince of Wales increased from 20 to 47. In South Western Sydney, the number increased from 118 to 180, including: Bankstown Hospital – 15 to 30 Campbelltown Hospital – 37 to 54 Liverpool Hospital – 22 to 52. In Western Sydney, the number increased from 99 to 111, including: Blacktown Hospital – 17 to 22 Westmead Hospital – 50 to 62. In Sydney Local Health District, the number increased from 62 to 114, including: RPA – 11 to 29 Canterbury Hospital – 8 to 25. Aged Care Response Package The NSW Government is investing $35.7 million into an Aged Care Response Package, to deliver much-needed relief for older people experiencing discharge delays. The NSW Government is also working with the Commonwealth to expand services helping older people remain well and safely at home, reducing avoidable hospital presentations and admissions. These initiatives include: Expanding Aged Care Outreach Services to provide short-term multidisciplinary care in the home to avoid unnecessary hospitalisations Rolling out Virtual Specialist Geriatric Care which delivers specialist geriatric support to people aged 65 years and over at home, helping to avoid hospital admissions and supporting earlier discharge where appropriate Hospital performance Despite these challenges, the Bureau of Health Information has released quarterly data which shows there has been some improvements in emergency department performance and the number of people accessing care outside of the hospital. The proportion of triage category two patients – people with life threatening conditions – being treated on time improved in the April to June 2026 quarter to 56.8 per cent compared to four years ago (51.6 per cent in 2022 under the former Liberal National Government), significantly improving in Western Sydney which increased from 25.1 per cent under the Liberals to 41 per cent. Notable hospitals which have improved the proportion of triage category two patients treated on time compared to four years ago include: Westmead – 31.4 per cent under the Liberals to 39 Blacktown – 10.6 per cent under the Liberals to 36.6 Campbelltown – 42.2 per cent under the Liberals to 65.8 Liverpool – 49.1 per cent under the Liberals to 65.8 St George – 26.6 per cent under the Liberals to 38.3 Nepean – 24.7 per cent under the Liberals to 33.7 Mount Druitt – 17.5 per cent under the Liberals to 46.1 The overall proportion of patients being treated on time improved in the April to June 2026 quarter to 68.7 per cent compared to four years ago (62.8 per cent in 2022 under the Liberals), including in Western Sydney which improved from 40.3 per cent to 56.5 over the same time period. Ramping has reduced in the April to June 2026 quarter with transfer of care from paramedics to the ED increasing to 80.3 per cent compared to four years ago (.5 per cent in 2022 under the Liberals). This coincides with an increase in calls to Healthdirect to almost 560,000 in the year to 30 June 2026 (up from 527,000 the previous year). Over half of these were diverted to non-ED healthcare – 60.7 per cent of calls, up from 56.4 per cent – including referrals to local GPs, virtual health care, urgent care and other health professionals. More hospitals, more beds, more staff, more services This improvement in performance coincides with an increased uptake of alternative pathways to care outside of the hospital, including Healthdirect, the expansion of virtual care services across NSW with $124 million invested for urgent care services; over $500 million invested into ED relief; more beds and the recruitment of more health workers including over 900 nurses, 740 paramedics, 1,400 doctors and 1,500 allied health workers over the past three years. We’re investing $10.3 billion to help recruit an additional 9,000 health workers, deliver record pay rises for nurses and midwives, expand services, including 33,000 more ED presentations and an additional 2,900 planned surgeries per year, as well as $11.9 billion to deliver 32 new and upgraded hospitals and more than 2,500 additional beds and treatment spaces across the state, including over 800 in Western Sydney. Quotes attributable to Minister for Health Ryan Park: “The number of people waiting for aged care and NDIS placements stranded in NSW hospitals is growing at an unprecedented and unsustainable level. “For the first time, NSW Health has confirmed that one in eight ED accessible beds in NSW public hospitals cannot be used as a result. “Waiting indefinitely in a hospital is not good for patient mobility, recovery or quality of life. “Despite these challenges, we are continuing to see progress in emergency department wait times which has coincided with a significant investment from the Minns Labor Government into ED relief – and I want to thank our health workers for their hard work and commitment to our health system.” Related ministerial articles Ministerial media release NSW Health Secretary Susan Pearce After more than 30 years of outstanding service to NSW Health, including almost five years as Secretary, Ms Susan Pearce AM has advised me of her intention to retire at the end of March 2027. records.body_text: Lasting Legacy: A new era for the Hunter as M1 extension opens | Prime Minister of Australia Skip to main content Lasting Legacy: A new era for the Hunter as M1 extension opens Media release Wednesday 9 September 2026 The Hon Anthony Albanese MP Prime Minister of Australia The Hon Chris Minns MP Premier of New South Wales The Hon Catherine King MP Minister for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government The Hon Jenny Aitchison MP New South Wales Minister for Roads New South Wales Minister for Regional Transport Listen After more than four million hours of construction, the Hunter’s largest road infrastructure project will open to traffic in the early hours of 11 September, delivering a new 15-kilometre motorway connection between Black Hill and Raymond Terrace. The opening of the M1 Pacific Motorway extension marks a major milestone for the Hunter, closing a missing link in the Sydney to Brisbane economic corridor and strengthening one of Australia’s most important freight routes. The M1 Pacific Motorway extension and Hexham Straight widening projects were jointly funded with a total investment of $2.24 billion – $1.79 billion from the Albanese Government and $448 million from the Minns Government. It builds on Labor’s long record of investment in transforming the Pacific Highway. Between 2007 and 2013, the former Federal Labor Government committed more than $8.7 billion to complete the duplication of the Pacific Highway and deliver bypasses of towns across New South Wales. Since coming to government in 2022, the Albanese Government has committed a further $266.4 million to finish the remaining upgrades along the corridor, in addition to its investment in the M1 extension. The new motorway will provide a direct connection between the M1 at Black Hill and Raymond Terrace, improving connections to jobs, businesses, communities and major regional infrastructure, including Newcastle Airport and the Port of Newcastle. For motorists, it means cutting travel times by seven to nine minutes during peak hours and removing up to 25,000 vehicles a day from local streets. For freight, it means a faster and more reliable connection through the Hunter and along the Sydney to Brisbane corridor. The project has also been a major investment in local jobs and skills, with 70 per cent of the workforce drawn from the Hunter region and 99 apprentices and trainees gaining experience on the project. More than 2,700 workers have helped deliver the extension, clocking up more than four million hours of work to get the motorway open around 18 months earlier than originally planned. Construction of the motorway has been delivered on a remarkable scale, including: More than 1.6 million cubic metres of earth moved – enough to fill around 650 Olympic-sized swimming pools More than 720,000 tonnes of rock imported and placed across the project Construction of 11 bridges, supported by 278 bridge piles and 863 bridge girders More than 520 kilometres of drainage and wick drains installed 96 per cent of construction waste diverted from landfill 435 habitat structures installed to support native wildlife After years of planning and construction, the M1 extension is now ready to become part of everyday life across the Hunter – delivering a new connection that will transform the movement of people and freight and support the region’s next era of growth. For more information about the M1 Pacific Motorway extension visit: https://caportal.com.au/tfnsw/m1rt . Quotes attributable to Prime Minister, Anthony Albanese: “Labor has a proud record of investing in the Pacific Highway and delivering the infrastructure regional communities need. “My Government is delivering a faster, safer connection through the Hunter and invested almost $1.8 billion in this project. “It means motorists will be able to travel from Melbourne all the way to Coffs Harbour without hitting a single traffic light or roundabout and we’re getting on with finishing the Coffs Harbour Bypass too. “This is what investing in infrastructure is all about. We’re cutting travel times, getting trucks and freight moving and building for the future.” Quotes attributable to Premier of New South Wales, Chris Minns: “This is a big day for the Hunter. After years of construction, this road is opening and people will feel the difference from day one. “It means shorter trips, less traffic on local roads and a much better connection between Newcastle, the Hunter and the rest of the state. “This project has been a mammoth undertaking, and I want to acknowledge the hundreds of local workers who have helped deliver this important connection for the Hunter. “This is about more than infrastructure. It’s about backing the Hunter and ensuring this great part of our state remains open for business.” Quotes attributable to Federal Minister for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government, Catherine King: “The days of holiday traffic crawling through the Hunter are over, with our new bypass of Hexham and Heatherbrae now delivered. “We committed to delivering this project back in 2019, we pushed the government of the day to get on with planning and we got work underway in 2023. “I want to thank the 2,700 workers who delivered this project. “We planned to open this project in 2028, they got it done one and a half years early.” Quotes attributable to NSW Minister for Roads, Jenny Aitchison: “On 11 September 2026, communities in the Hunter will wake up to a brand new 15km M1 motorway. “A project built by the very people it will serve, with 70 per cent of the workforce coming from right here in the region. “Almost 950,000 people are expected to call the Hunter home by 2041 and our roads have a vital role to play in how the region functions. “The M1 extension reflects the needs of a region that is working harder, building faster and more ambitious than ever. A road that will support families, workers, local businesses and our industries. “I am incredibly proud to see this mammoth investment into the Hunter be days from opening. “This is Labor delivering for the Hunter.” Quotes attributable to Federal Member for Paterson, Meryl Swanson: “Today is a really proud day for our community. People in Paterson knew this road was needed, but it was always the next promise, never the next project. When we came to Government in 2022, we turned years of talk into action. "Not only are we delivering the M1 Extension to Raymond Terrace, we're opening it more than a year ahead of schedule - funded, fast-tracked and delivered. That's what happens when governments work together, back our region and get on with the job. "This project belongs to the thousands of local workers who helped make it happen. From the engineers and planners to the crews on the ground, thank you. As I always say, Hunter workers work harder, and this road is proof of that.” Quotes attributable to Federal Member for Newcastle, Sharon Claydon: “This completed link secures Newcastle as the economic centre of the Hunter by keeping freight as well as general traffic moving safer and smoother in all directions for years to come. “After providing a massive boost to local jobs with more than four million hours of construction, the finished motorway now becomes a permanent and reliable pathway for industrial growth across the Hunter.” Quotes attributable to State Member for Port Stephens, Kate Washington: “Woohoo! The Hexham bottleneck is gone for good! “This is a great day for the people of Port Stephens, who have been looking forward to this day for decades. “Many locals travel on this stretch daily, so it’s going to make a massive difference to their lives – getting where we need to go smarter, faster and safer.” Quotes attributable to State Member for Wallsend, Sonia Hornery: “This is a huge day for the Wallsend electorate and our surrounding suburbs. “After years of waiting, we finally get a motorway that takes pressure off our local streets and gives our community room to breathe. “I can't wait to see the difference this makes - not just for the daily commute, but for local businesses, for families heading off on a weekend away, and for a community that has waited a long time for this moment.” Quotes attributable to State Member for Newcastle, Tim Crakanthorp: “Newcastle's future runs through this motorway. “Quicker, more reliable access to the Port and the Airport means our exporters and industries can compete on time, not just on price. “Along with the newly completed Hexham Straight Widening project, this will improve travel times for all Newcastle and Hunter commuters. “This is the kind of infrastructure that keeps Newcastle’s economy growing for decades to come.” Share

records.body_text: My Feed, My Way | Prime Minister of Australia Skip to main content My Feed, My Way Media release Tuesday 8 September 2026 The Hon Anthony Albanese MP Prime Minister of Australia The Hon Anika Wells MP Minister for Communications Minister for Sport Listen The Albanese Government is taking the next step following its world leading social media age ban to ensure Australians have more choice online, with draft legislation for the Digital Duty of Care released today for targeted consultation. These new laws will put the onus on digital service providers to provide a safe online environment, setting minimum standards for the features and tools they use. This will include an Australian first, “My Feed, My Way,” initiative which will give Australians control over their social media algorithms. Social media platforms will be required to send a notification to new and existing users offering them a choice over their default feed. Users can choose to opt in to having their default feed include personalised content recommended by the algorithm. Alternatively, users can opt out of personally recommended content in their default feed and see the friends and creators they choose to follow. This will give Australians greater choice over their platforms and what they see. Further, digital services like online games, apps and AI chatbots will be required to protect under 18s from design features that have negative behavioural impacts, like addictive features or those that can have an effect on a young person’s self-esteem. They will also be required to protect under 18s from harmful content like: content that promotes, encourages or accelerates eating disorders content that promotes hostile ideas about women and gender equality pornography content that glorifies crime or life endangering stunts content that causes serious mental health distress, including abuse and bullying. Australians will benefit from better protection from seriously harmful and illegal content across digital services, and social media users will be afforded more choice. The draft laws provide eSafety with the power to issue removal notices for nudify apps or websites, and streamline the child cyber-bulling and adult cyber abuse schemes to enable eSafety to deal more quickly with this harmful material. Digital platforms will be required to document the measures taken to address identified risks of harm to Australian users and ensure these measures remain effective over time. Failure to comply with the Duty of Care could attract penalties of up to $109.2 million, with the independent eSafety Commissioner responsible for compliance and enforcement. The Government is seeking feedback from digital platforms, industry bodies, civil society organisations and advocates on the draft laws, with legislation to be introduced to Parliament this year. Quotes attributable to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese “This is not about giving government control, it is about giving people control. “Today we are releasing the government’s approach to give Australians choice over their online experience, “My Feed, My Way.” “Australia is leading the world with our social media age ban and online safety approach. “This work has been led by parents and advocates and we have backed them. We will continue to do so.” Quotes attributable to Minister for Communications Anika Wells “Just as we have basic safety standards for cars, toys or food, the duty of care applies basic standards for the online products we use every day. “The duty of care goes beyond social media to ensure children are protected from harmful content and features, including on chatbots and gaming platforms, apps and messaging platforms. “It will also give parents the tools they need to keep their family safe online. “When it comes to social media, Australians over the age of 16 will be able to opt in or opt out of the algorithm easily. The duty of care will require platforms to give users over 16 choice on what feed they see when they open the app – and to respect that choice. “The digital duty of care will ensure online service providers – including some of the most powerful companies in the world – step up and do more to keep Australians safe from harm on their platforms.” Share

records.body_text: Press conference - Tarro, NSW | Prime Minister of Australia Skip to main content Press conference - Tarro, NSW Transcript Wednesday 9 September 2026 The Hon Anthony Albanese MP Prime Minister of Australia Listen MERYL SWANSON, MEMBER FOR PATERSON : Well, good morning everyone and welcome to the M1 here at – well, we’re kind of at Tarro at the moment, but it’s on its way to Raymond Terrace. But what is most exciting is that the people of the Hunter and the people of New South Wales and the Eastern Seaboard of Australia are going to be on their way within 48 hours on this magnificent piece of road infrastructure. Success has many parents, but let me tell you, Labor has delivered this road. And I cannot wait for the people of Australia to be driving on it in less than 48 hours. It’s been coming for around 20 years, and we’ve all been working towards this day to have it officially opened. It’s opened under Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and we were just reflecting – I’ve been in this job ten years, and I think I’ve spoken in Parliament about this officially about 40 times, and I’ve mentioned it many more times. And I remember saying when I first got the job, I said 'the M1 is terrible. It's terrible at Hexham. It's just a choke point between Sydney and Brisbane. It needs to be fixed.' And he has backed this project in every step of the way. And I want to also mention Minister Catherine King. She came here and said 'we're going to fast track it.' It’s one thing to make a promise, it's another thing to deliver it. And that big group of people behind us, those workers, 70 per cent of them are from the Hunter. They've delivered this project not only on budget, but over 12 months early. When do you hear that? Especially in construction in the last few years. We've done it. The rubber is going to hit the road. It is an awesome day. And I want to thank my state counterpart, Jenny Aitchison and Kate Washington as well. It's a big team Labor effort, but it's a big effort for our community. Thank you, thank you, thank you and I can't wait to be driving on it. Ladies and gentlemen, I want to welcome the Prime Minister as well. Thanks, PM. ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER : Thanks very much, Meryl. And congrats to you. You've been a champion for this road, as have the other locals who are joining us here today. Sharon Claydon, the Member for Newcastle. Tim Crakanthorp, the state Member for Newcastle. We have Kate Washington, the Member for Port Stephens. And of course as well, Jenny Aitchison, who's also the Minister, along with Minister King as well. This will make an enormous difference, and I've been very passionate for my entire political career about fixing the Pacific Highway. My name is Anthony, I'm named after my cousin who was four years old, who died on the Pacific Highway just before I was born back in 1963. And the tragedies that have occurred on the Pacific Highway, up and down, is something that drove me to be very passionate about fixing the Pac Highway. And we put in $7.6 billion of infrastructure upgrades including just north of here to Taree. The projects like the Kempsey Bypass, T to E, up further north. All of the projects that made sure that the duplication of this highway was turned into something that some people thought would never ever happen into now a reality. So, that when this road opens in less than 48 hours, we will have no traffic lights all the way from Melbourne right up to Coffs Harbour. And later this year you'll be able to go to the Queensland border. And I want to pay tribute to all those locals who've campaigned, particularly here in the Hunter. I want to thank all the workers who've delivered this project on budget or under budget and more than 12 months ahead of time. For infrastructure projects, that is a remarkable achievement, and this road will make an enormous difference. Everyone who's ever driven from Sydney to Brisbane or locals in this area will all know that this choke point that occurred when you got to Hexham and Heatherbrae and these areas was something that was a real issue. This is good for productivity, it's good for freight, it's good for people travelling on this road, but it's also great for locals because what it will do is make sure that it separates out the highway from local roads, which is good for road safety. It's also been great for jobs. 70 per cent of the workers who worked on this project, worth about $2.4 billion, an 80:20 split from the Commonwealth to the state government, have been locals. And as well as that, the local suppliers as well, who've supplied the works that have gone in here, has made an enormous difference. The Hunter has an incredible future. This comes just a couple of weeks after I was at Tomago, announcing with the state government to make sure that that facility will continue to drive aluminium production, which will make such a difference. It comes on top of the state government's commitment to build trains here in the Hunter. We want manufacturing here, we want jobs here, we want a strong economy here. And we're working with the Minns Labor Government to make sure that that occurs. This will be a great day on Friday. I am so proud the work that we have done. I'm unashamedly an infrastructure nerd. It's been my concentration in the 30 years in which I've been in public life, because I know that it is good infrastructure that drives our economy, drives productivity, and that is precisely what this project will do. I'll hand to the Infrastructure Minister, Catherine King. CATHERINE KING, MINISTER FOR INFRASTRUCTURE : Thanks very much. It is fantastic to be back here with both state and parliamentary colleagues, but also the Prime Minister who basically started this project off when he was Infrastructure Minister the last time we were in government, and I'm so proud that now gets to cut the ribbon on what is an amazing project here on the M1. As the Prime Minister has said, once Coffs is open towards the end of this year, depending on the weather, you will be able to drive from the Victorian border to the Queensland border with no traffic lights at all. This takes out five sets of traffic lights, but of course removes a really significant pinch point that has been the bane of the local community for some time, but really does provide that connection right the way through to the Queensland border and of course through to Victoria. I well remember Meryl and I standing under the bridge in 2019, when we weren't in government, saying this project needed to be fast tracked. We then had to wait, unfortunately, until we got into government in 2022 and we came and turned the sod in 2023 to get this project actually started. It has taken Labor governments to actually deliver this project and that is what we are doing for the Hunter right the way across the board. Whether it is the Singleton Bypass – again, another significant piece of infrastructure for this region that will be open again hopefully this year, depending on the weather, we're pretty close to doing that as well – Muswellbrook starting as well. Really significant investments in infrastructure through the Hunter, and of course our investments in the future of high-speed rail. I really do want to congratulate all of the workers here. Well over 2,700 workers supporting local businesses, 70 per cent of them here. They have done an amazing job. It's a piece of infrastructure to which they and their families can be very proud because residents will be driving on this for many, many years to come. And it's a great day for the Hunter and I can't wait to see, I'm sure Meryl is going to post a video of driving along. Not her driving while she takes the video, I'm sure, but driving along this magnificent piece of road on Friday when it opens and I really hope every single Member enjoys that experience. I'll hand over to Jenny. JENNY AITCHISON : Thanks, Catherine. Look, what a historic day to be here. It was way back in 1928 that the highway between Hexham and Tweed was proclaimed State Highway Number 10. And in that time since then, 98 years, we have bypassed 30 towns. This was always one of the most difficult with Coffs Harbour because of the terrain. We have a 14-kilometre bypass here that goes in this massive viaduct, three and a half kilometres over the Hunter River. A significant engineering feat. The workers, the 2,700 workers who work on this site are part of an amazing transformation of our national highway. The genesis of this project, the Pacific Highway upgrade, started with that horrific crash in 1989, those two horrific crashes where 57 people died. This is about improving the safety, first and foremost, of this iconic and vital infrastructure for our nation. We know that until that Pacific Highway program started, with Labor government signing in 1996 to commence this upgrade, we wouldn't be here today. And as the Prime Minister and Minister King have both said, this languished on the books in New South Wales and was ignored for over a decade. It took that federal contribution, that 80 per cent injection, to actually get it moving. And what we see today is a project that is well ahead of time. If you look at the signs all around us, they say due to be completed in 2028. Well, it's 2026, and here we are. In 48 hours, we'll be driving on it. I'm incredibly proud of the work that every single one of the workers here has undertaken to ensure that we got to today ahead of schedule. I'm really grateful to our communities who have worked with us to enable us to get that work done. These projects are not easy. They have a massive disruption. But people could see the promise of this. Hexham has been the bugbear. You go down to the Transport Management Centre on any long weekend, and this is the intersection that all of them are looking at and trying to work out how we're going to get people through. Any flood – in those terrible floods last year, it was taking an hour to get that few kilometres down the road. This will be a massive game changer for our region. 25,000 cars use this on a normal day, but we know during those peak times it's even more. We know this will help to relieve a lot of that congestion around the surrounding areas, particularly in Thornton, which has really suffered from having to take up the load of not having this road done in time, which it should have been. I'm so grateful to the Albanese Labor government, the Minns Labor government and all of my colleagues across the Hunter who have advocated for this infrastructure, the workers who have done it, as we've said, 70 per cent of them here, local, 99 apprentices and trainees have learnt their trade on this job. That's an incredible legacy for them. I want to thank our Aboriginal elders and our communities here to who have engaged with us on the project. It is important that we acknowledge they are the knowledge holders of our nation's trading routes and our journeys and places of meaning. And without them we would not be where we are today. I want to thank everyone and I'm going to pass over to Kate. KATE WASHINGTON : Thanks, Jenny. And good morning, everyone. I know that this is a project of national and state significance, but on behalf of the people of Port Stephens, can I just say, woohoo! The Hexham bottleneck is gone for good. Honestly, this is just, it has been the bugbear of our community for so long and I know it has impacted so many other people from across the state. And the country. But literally locals spend so much time travelling this stretch every single day to go to work, to go to sporting events, to see their kids go and play footy. This is going to make a massive difference to the daily lives of locals here in Port Stephens and across the Hunter. So, we are super excited. We were all gritting our teeth with the 2028 end time on this project. Now that it is 2026 and we are standing here opening it, it is just a remarkable feat. So, I'm really grateful to the Albanese Government, Minns Labor Government, Minister King, Minister Aitchison and all of my federal and state colleagues. We have been working together on this for some time and to see it happen now, it's going to be an enormous game changer for the Hunter, for Port Stephens. And honestly, we are taking off here in the Hunter. There are so many good things happening and this M1 was a critical part of the puzzle that we needed to make happen. And thanks to all of the people that are around me now, but particularly the workers behind us. That has been an incredible achievement. I want to thank my community for their patience through the construction period. But big, enormous gratitude to the workforce that has made this happen on budget and well, well ahead of schedule. My community could not be more grateful. Thanks so much. JOURNALIST : Prime Minister, the [INAUDIBLE] took place back in 1989 after a terrible bus crash. Made recommendations of which in 1996, the Commonwealth came in and put a lot of money into the Pacific Highway. Obviously, we've reached a milestone at the moment with this particular project at Coffs Harbour. But there are several major intersections up the Coast requiring an injection of funds. Will you be committing more funding to the Pacific Highway upgrade in terms of building those six or seven interchanges that are required to be built? PRIME MINISTER : Well, with respect, the fact is between 1996 and 2007 there was $1.3 billion put into this road. We put in, in the next six years, $7.6 billion. Over half the time, we put in six times the funding, because it took the election of a Labor government to actually get the real investment through. And we continue to be major investors. We brought forward additional funding for this project. We brought forward as well the funding to make sure the Coffs Harbour Bypass was able to be completed. We'll continue to invest in infrastructure. I'll ask my Minister if she wants anything to add. But once we get the Coffs Harbour Bypass open, then that will be traffic light free the whole way through from Melbourne right through to the Queensland border. So, where there have been issues such as Banora Point, T to E, the whole way down the Coast. The area north of Coffs was a big issue as well. Around Woolgoolga up to Arrawarra. All of this road, I know every inch of it. And under my Prime Ministership it will certainly always be looked after, including the choke points. MINISTER KING : Thanks very much for the question. First, we're celebrating an incredible milestone here and that substantial investment that has come again started under Prime Minister Albanese, finished under Prime Minister Albanese. It's a terrific tribute. We get requests from state governments. As you can see with this project in particular, we work very closely as the delivery partner, as the co-investor for infrastructure. We get requests from state governments. If there are further projects, which there always are – I want to build everything all at once, all the time. We'd love to be able to do that. But there are always requests from state governments. They go through our usual budget processes, and we'll consider those as they come forward. So, if there are further projects that need to come forward either from the Queensland Government, on the Queensland side, from the NSW Government or from the Victorian Government, we of course will consider those very seriously as part of our budget processes. JOURNALIST : A few questions to you, Prime Minister. Did your office identify the Marrickville Golf Club for funding as part of the major and local community infrastructure program? PRIME MINISTER : Well, I answered this on the ABC before. The fact is that the Inner West Council own the golf club. There were three grants given to my electorate. One of those was for the Leichhardt Women's Health Centre. That's a women's health centre that's been there since the 1970s. It's on the corner of a residential street in Leichardt. They've been providing services to women, health services, for 50 years. It's aged. What that funding was about was for assisting the upgrade of that. The second grant was for St Vincent de Paul for a refuge for women and children escaping domestic violence, for the upgrade there. The third grant is for an Inner West Council owned golf club that's been there for a very long period of time. And what that golf course does is, it's a community facility. But importantly, because it's really old, they have septic tank, it's on a flooded area on the banks of the Cooks River and when it rains, raw sewage goes into the river. It's been something that's been identified as an issue for a long period of time. We're funding it, we're fixing it. That's what good governments do. JOURNALIST : But, Prime Minister, these, I understand, were an invite only grant, so was it you or your office personally that recommended this project? PRIME MINISTER : No, no. It was an election commitment, an election commitment that we're delivering, because we're a good government and when we say we'll do something, like this road, we bring forward funding. And you know, the ABC have been told this, they've chosen not to report it in the way in which the facts are there. This is a par 62 local golf course which is used on some days. They use it to close off the first fairway because people go and have picnics by the river. There are – as the ABC has reported, I did campaign to keep the golf course available because I didn't want that really important space, of which there isn't enough in the Inner West for people to enjoy amenity. I make no apologies for that, like I make no apologies for supporting the Greenway project and other projects in my electorate. JOURNALIST : Just on another matter concerning the Hunter. You just approved the Central Queensland Mine extension. Does this mean anything in regards to the Hunter Valley HVO proposed extension? PRIME MINISTER : No. It means these things are all done on their merits. Thank you. We've got to get on. Raymond Terrace M1 Extension; Delivery of Election Commitments. Share

records.body_text: Television interview - ABC news breakfast | Prime Minister of Australia Skip to main content Television interview - ABC news breakfast Transcript Wednesday 9 September 2026 The Hon Anthony Albanese MP Prime Minister of Australia Listen JAMES GLENDAY, HOST : Well, the Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is out and about this morning and he's happy to say that he's joining us live from north of Newcastle on a road. Prime Minister, welcome back to the program. It's a Sitting Week in Canberra but you've skipped town. Why are you up near Newcastle? ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER : Because this piece of highway that I'm on that'll open on Friday, just north of Newcastle, travelling 15 kilometres to Raymond Terrace – everyone who's ever driven from Sydney to Brisbane or in this region knows that when you hit areas like Hexham and Heatherbrae, you hit a traffic jam. Now this will mean that there are no traffic lights all the way there from Melbourne till you get to Coffs Harbour. And when the Coffs Harbour Bypass opens later this year, it'll be all the way through to the Queensland border. This road we'll open today, but traffic starts in two days’ time, and it's going to make such a difference for productivity, for road safety, for everyone who travels on this road, but importantly as well for locals because it'll take a lot of the traffic off those local roads. So, great for road safety as well. GLENDAY : You do love infrastructure. I appreciate you joining us this morning – PRIME MINISTER : I do. GLENDAY : Now we've been getting plenty of questions about your social media plans. Do you know what percentage of people are actually likely to choose to opt out of a default algorithm on a social media app? PRIME MINISTER : Well, it's up to them. This is going to be world first. So, we'll say to them that's fine, that's up to them if they're adults, but the power will be back in their hands, which is what the ‘My Feed, My Way’ plan is all about. GLENDAY : I just wonder if social media giants will still have quite a lot of power here. They've sort of done this elsewhere in the world. What are you going to do if they respond by making non-algorithm versions of their apps so clunky, so awful that people feel well, ‘I've got no choice but to go back to the standard algorithm version’? PRIME MINISTER : Well, we'll deal with these issues as we go through. What we've done is we've released an exposure draft yesterday. We have learned some of the lessons as well, have been learned and acted on in the way that the draft legislation is there. The eSafety Commissioner will be able to examine this on an ongoing basis. But we think this is the right thing to do. We'll introduce the legislation in October. We're hoping to get very broad support for this legislation. And it's responding to the needs of Australians. Organisations like Teach Us Consent have been fantastic in the role that they've played. This is change from the bottom up. This is government listening and acting in the interests of Australians rather than in the interests of these tech giants. GLENDAY : Just to another issue. I'm sure you've seen this story the ABC has it on the top of its website about alleged pork barrelling by your government. Do you have an honorary membership to the Marrickville Golf Club and have you declared it? PRIME MINISTER : I'm very glad that you've asked this question. You know what? There's three grants in my electorate. One of them is for Leichhardt Women's Health Centre. That's one of the first women's health centres that was ever established in Australia, specifically helping women. It's in an old terrace. It's been there since the 1970s and it's for the upgrade of that. The second grant – GLENDAY : I'm sure they did very important work. Can I just take you back to my question, though – do you have a membership? PRIME MINISTER : Well, the second grant – well, I'll give you the answer. The second grant is for St. Vincent's, and what that is as St. Vincent's de Paul, for a shelter for women and children escaping domestic violence. The third grant is for the Inner West Council, who own the Marrickville Golf Course and run it at the moment. It's a course that's been there a long time. It's a public course. It's used by lots of community members, back to 19 – for many, many years. It's a par 62, so it's available to everyone, it’s a community facility – GLENDAY : I've seen you praising it. I've seen you talk about how much you like it – PRIME MINISTER : And what it's for – yeah, and what it's for, what it's for, because the ABC were told information they chose not to publish appropriately. What it's for, is for at the moment because it's on a flood area by the Cooks River, when it rains and there's flooding, raw sewage goes into the Cooks River. That's what it's for, for fixing that. I make no apologies for my electorate being serviced by me as a good local member. These three grants are all appropriate. Apparently about fifteen years ago, to go – and the ABC were told this – fifteen years ago, apparently someone said – GLENDAY: So, yes, we're going to get to – you do have a membership? PRIME MINISTER : No, I don't have a membership. Fifteen years ago they gave an honorary membership. You know how much membership costs apparently, according to the article? Apparently it cost five bucks to join. I don't play golf. I'm a tennis player rather than a golf player. And like a lot of organisations in my seat, a lot of clubs, local community based things, they say, ‘oh, we'll give the local member honorary membership’. Apparently that happened fifteen years ago or something. I haven't been into the clubhouse for many, many years. And the ABC chose to to do this. That's up to them. But I make no apologies for the fact that this was fixed. GLENDAY: So, should you have declared this though, or did you just not even know that you were an honorary member? PRIME MINISTER : No. How would I – fifteen years ago someone decided to say, ‘oh, we'll make him an honorary member’. I don't have a card. I don't go in there. I haven't been in there for years. I used to walk my dog along the path, as lots of people do because it's a community club. The ABC were told this. GLENDAY : We'll move on. Can I ask you – PRIME MINISTER: And the ABC should do better. GLENDAY : Thank you for that feedback, Prime Minister. We appreciate all the feedback we get. What's happening in the Solomon Islands – PRIME MINISTER: Very direct feedback. GLENDAY : Are you, have you reached a nearly billion dollar deal to try to shore up the fairly fragile leadership of the country's Prime Minister, Matthew Wale? PRIME MINISTER : You know what I do when I negotiate with countries? I negotiate with them and with their leaders. I don't do it on the ABC, with respect. GLENDAY : Fair enough. Is the reporting on these text messages wrong? Is that something else you'd like to correct about the ABC? PRIME MINISTER : No, we're in discussions. The ABC should stand up for the national interest. That's what I do. And for the national interests, I'll engage on behalf of Australia to make sure we defend our interests and I'll continue to do so. We have a range of agreements. We've reached alliances with Papua New Guinea and with Fiji, agreements with Vanuatu, with Nauru. We have said very clearly, we're in discussions with the Solomon Islands with Prime Minister Wale, and we look forward to successfully completing those discussions. GLENDAY : We'll watch this space. And I would add, I think the ABC does stand up for the national interest. Prime Minister, can I ask you, there's another ABC story about the battery program that the government has. The Opposition wants an inquiry because there are allegations of fraud. Is that something you will entertain? PRIME MINISTER : Look that, they really don't like renewables, do they? They really don't. We have had now something like 530,000 households and small businesses have installed batteries. That's good for them. What that does is lower their power bills, many of them, to zero. And meaning that they're putting energy back into the grid, means that every Australian is benefiting because it takes the pressure off the grid during peak times. This has been a fantastically successful program. They've opposed it, like they oppose all renewables. They wanted an expensive nuclear scheme – GLENDAY: That sounds like a no. PRIME MINISTER: Well, we stand up for – this program has been incredibly successful. GLENDAY : Just, just finally, Prime Minister, because we've got to let you go – those who know you say that you're a really tough competitor. A mortgage broker who openly hates your budget and joined the Liberal Party as a result, recently won an auction for a tennis game against you. Apparently brought over some friends who also don't like your budget. How did the meeting in the match go? PRIME MINISTER : Well, the match went pretty well. It was very successful. And it was for charity. That's the main thing. GLENDAY : What was the score? PRIME MINISTER : 6-0, 6-0, 6-0. And it was, it was, you know, it was, it was what it was. But for me the main point was that it was raising funds for charity. I think it would have been good if the gentleman had put some of the money he's put into billboards and skywriting and all of that, given additional money to St. Vincent's, to Red Kite, a charity that provides support for the families of children who have cancer. It was for a very good cause. GLENDAY : He spent 16 grand on the meeting. Did he convince you of anything? PRIME MINISTER : He spent a lot, he spent a lot more than that on billboards and other things as well. So, he's going, okay. GLENDAY: Prime Minister, we have to let you go. We do appreciate your time. PRIME MINISTER : Thanks very much. ENDS E&OE Raymond Terrace M1 Extension; Digital Duty of Care; My Feed, My Way; Delivery of Election Commitments; Solomon Islands; Cheaper Home Batteries; Charity Tennis Match. Share

records.body_text: Television interview - Sunrise | Prime Minister of Australia Skip to main content Television interview - Sunrise Transcript Wednesday 9 September 2026 The Hon Anthony Albanese MP Prime Minister of Australia Listen MATT SHIRVINGTON, HOST : Well, the way that each and every Australian uses social media could be about to change forever. Every Aussie may soon have the power to opt out of algorithms online. There are the systems that analyse massive amounts of online data to feed you the posts that will be keeping you scrolling. NAT BARR, HOST : Under the proposed new laws, social media companies would have to give users a choice over whether they want to be shown that recommended content or just posts from people they follow. For more, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese joins us now. Tell us, how will you force the tech giants to do this and do it properly? Because I guess we're still seeing 80 per cent or so of teens still on social media despite the under-16s ban. How will this be different? ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER : We want to make sure we get the legislation right. We've got further strengthening of our social media laws going through Parliament, hopefully today through the Senate. But when it comes to My Feed, My Way , this is about putting the power back in the hands of your listeners so that they get to decide what they see. So, a pop up that will say you want to continue to receive the algorithms or you want to opt out and receive the feed from people who you follow or people who you want to see it from. This is about putting the power back in Australians’ hands and away from the tech giants who of course we know that this is causing massive issues and many of your listeners will be concerned about what people have access to. We know that within a period of just literally minutes, people who go online can often be fed quite dangerous material, pornography, a range of things that they don't really want to see going down those rabbit holes. And this is about empowering Australians. It's as simple as that. BARR : It sounds good. What if the social media companies don't play ball? There have been no fines issued and all the kids seem to still be on social media. PRIME MINISTER : Well, there have been no fines issued because the power of the eSafety Commissioner hasn't been strong enough. That's why we've legislated for that, to enable that, as well as a doubling of the fines. That's the legislation that's before the Senate. It was delayed, it could have been passed months ago, but hopefully it'll be passed today. This will provide for fines of $100 million to make sure that there is compliance with this. We want to make sure that power's back in the hands of Australians. And this is something the whole world, of course, is grappling with, with the increase in mental health issues, eating disorders, the increased behavioural issues we're seeing from young men when it comes to some of the things that they get exposed to, that somehow they see as normal, the increased incidence lead to tragedies we've seen of choking, for example, is something that we just need to take action on. It's not easy – SHIRVINGTON : Something needs to change. PRIME MINISTER : – but it’s the right thing to do. It's the right thing to do. And Australia once again is leading the world. SHIRVINGTON : Moving on. $34 billion has been wiped off from the housing market in the June quarter, and home values are expected to decline even further into next year. Are these the results that you wanted with your changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax? PRIME MINISTER : Look, housing prices as of August are higher nationally than they were last August, a year ago. What we saw was a drop in house prices in recent times. There's a range of factors which are there, including, of course, interest rates is a factor there. What we want is a comprehensive plan for housing supply. And of course, when it comes to capital gains, negative gearing, people can still engage in that if they wish to pursue an investment, but it's for new builds, and that's about feeding into new housing supply, because we're throwing everything at the housing issue. We know that the housing system was bust. You had a 400 per cent increase in house prices since these changes were put in place in 1999. That's just not sustainable, and we want young people to get a fair crack. I don't want to lead a country where home ownership is not possible. And that is where we were headed, which is why we've taken this action. BARR : Yeah, look, house prices might be up overall across the country, but it's being held up by the smaller cities. It might be hard to talk to people in Sydney and Melbourne about their houses going up in the last year. PRIME MINISTER : I don't think your listeners in Perth think they're a small city. So, anyway. BARR : They know that. Finally, we just had your tennis opponent, Joseph Daoud, on. He just accused you of, quote, manufacturing your winning score in that tennis match you played with him yesterday. What's your response to that, Prime Minister? PRIME MINISTER : Well, look, you know, we played a match. It was for charity. Importantly, the score was 6-0, 6-0, 6-0. It was played in good spirits. Importantly, it raised money for charity. I just wish that Joseph had put some of the money he put into billboards and into skywriting and into all the other things, into Redkite or into the charities, which was what it was for. But that's a decision for him. SHIRVINGTON : PM, he said you had a 15-minute tinkle. What were you doing in the 15 minutes during the match? BARR : That’s a personal question. PRIME MINISTER : I've never been asked that, Matt. SHIRVINGTON : He said you used the word tinkle. PRIME MINISTER : Well, I said to him after the second set, and it was actually 1-0. I waited for the break. Change of ends. I said, I'll just go have a tinkle. As you do. SHIRVINGTON : 15 minutes. PRIME MINISTER : It was about two minutes, Matt. And there's a range of stories that he's had in interviews. They vary from interview to interview. It's hard to keep up. Matt. Let me just say this. SHIRVINGTON : Charity was the real winner, but it was 6-0, 6-0, 6-0. PRIME MINISTER : Charity was the winner, but the score was pretty clear as well. And you know, the discussion, the couple of people he brought along as well, I'm not sure if they were known to him or what the connection was, but they were delightful and I was very pleased to host them accommodate at The Lodge for a number of good causes. BARR : Prime Minister, thank you for your time this morning. PRIME MINISTER : Thanks very much, guys. ENDS E&OE My Feed, My Way; Housing; Charity Tennis Match. Share

records.body_text: Television interview - Today | Prime Minister of Australia Skip to main content Television interview - Today Transcript Wednesday 9 September 2026 The Hon Anthony Albanese MP Prime Minister of Australia Listen TOM STEINFORT, HOST: Well, the Labor Government is once again waging war on tech giants, releasing a draft Digital Duty of Care bill that allows Australians to opt out of addictive algorithms. SYLVIA JEFFREYS, HOST: To discuss, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese joins us now from New South Wales. Good morning to you, PM, and thank you for your time. ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning, great to be with you. JEFFREYS: Look, no doubt a lot of parents will be happy about some of these changes. But how can you guarantee the tech giants will comply? PRIME MINISTER: What we can do is make sure that we pass laws that ensure that the tech giants do have to comply. This is about putting the power back in the hands of consumers. And with the My Feed, My Way plan, what it's aimed at is if you want to go and continue to scroll and use the algorithms, you can do so. But if you want to opt out, you can certainly do so as well. This is about putting power back in the hands of Australians because we know that these big tech giants are having an impact. So, just one example is that you can have chatbots advising young girls and women on how to live on 600 calories a day. We know that that is just unhealthy, it's dangerous and it leads to eating disorders. And we want to make sure that that sort of behaviour doesn't occur. So, the government is prepared to pass this law. We've released an exposure draft just yesterday, and I think this is something the whole world is grappling with, frankly. But families watching this program are certainly grappling with it as well. STEINFORT : Well, I think everyone across the board agrees something needs to be done on this front. I guess it's the how that raises contention. The Coalition has flagged that its big concern is that Communications Minister, Anika Wells will be the one that has the power to determine what is and isn't harmful content. Matt Canavan was on before saying that it's like getting you to referee a Bunnies' match. Why die on that hill? Why wouldn't you just hand the power on that issue solely to an independent body, perhaps the eSafety Commissioner? PRIME MINISTER: Well, the eSafety Commissioner will of course, provide the advice. But Matt Canavan actually knows that he's been disingenuous, because all of these things will be disallowable. That is, it will be up to the whole Parliament, like the other previous laws have been. Otherwise, what you've got to do in order to make a change is to change the legislation so to be coming forward over and over again every time Parliament sits. JEFFREYS: Okay, but why not only hand that power to the eSafety Commissioner, rather than allowing Anika Wells, the Communications Minister, to have a say on what is and what is not harmful content, therefore opening the door for this discussion around censorship? PRIME MINISTER: The whole Parliament has a say. The whole Parliament. And under these laws, this isn't about censorship. This isn't about giving Anika Wells power. This is about giving your listeners power and people on their devices having the power themselves to either opt in or opt out. It's that simple. And the Coalition, a number of Liberal Party members, have supported this already. And Matt Canavan's in a position, competing with One Nation, as they do, of saying no to everything at the moment. But we're hoping that there be constructive engagement on this. We want this to pass with the support of the whole Parliament, because it should. Because this affects all Australians and it's about putting the power back in their hands. STEINFORT : All right, we'll turn now to other news, Prime Minister. The tobacco war is obviously something that's been bubbling along for years now. The Coalition and One Nation have got on the front foot pledging these huge cuts to the tax on tobacco. I know that your government has said that it won't go that far. But would you consider cutting the excise in part to try and reduce the issue that's, as I said, just not going away? PRIME MINISTER: Look, we've increased the excise by 34 per cent since we've been in government. It increased by 215 per cent while the Coalition were in government. What we want to do is to make sure that we continue to put that downward pressure on smoking rates. And making vapes available everywhere isn't going to help that. We also understand – STEINFORT : So you won't reduce the excise, is that what you're saying? You’re ruling that out? PRIME MINISTER: What we're saying is the big thing that we have to do is to crack down on crime. And you would have seen the massive seizure that occurred in the Northern Territory - STEINFORT : That hasn't been working, Prime Minister. We've been seeing that for quite some now. PRIME MINISTER: Well, it is. Yesterday you saw that massive exposure and crackdown in the Northern Territory with arrests with the Australian Federal Police with Border Security making sure that these are seized. We don't want to wave the white flag when it comes to criminals and we want to crack down on that. JEFFREYS: Ok, so sorry, just to answer that, to get to the bottom of that question that Tom asked. Are you saying you guarantee there will be no cut to the tobacco excise under a Labor government? PRIME MINISTER: No, what I'm guaranteeing is we'll take on the criminals. That’s what we’re doing, and we know that - JEFFREYS: So, you're open to a tax cut on tobacco? PRIME MINISTER: No, what we know what we're saying is what we're open to is to cracking down on criminals. That is what we are concentrating on. We're not about to wave the white flag. State governments as well have a responsibility to crack down on shops that are selling illegal products. We have upped, with a considerable increase, with hundreds of millions of dollars making sure that customs is taking action, border security, making sure that those issues are dealt with as well. Because we don't want to say, oh, it's okay for criminals to engage in this action. STEINFORT : All right, Prime Minister, finally, I guess we should ask why you're standing on the middle of a road today. PRIME MINISTER: Yeah, well, this is going to be fantastic. On Friday, I'm standing here at Raymond Terrace where the M1 will open - 15 kilometres of new road. Anyone who's driven from Sydney to Brisbane or vice versa will have hit the bottleneck when you hit the area on the Hunter here. And this new road will mean that it is traffic light free from Melbourne all the way to Coffs Harbour. Coffs Harbour bypass will open hopefully later this year, which will mean you go all the way to the Queensland border. So, this will be a big benefit to people here in the Hunter, but a big benefit as well for productivity in our economy and for road safety as well. JEFFREYS: I can't believe you missed an opportunity to wear high vis, Prime Minister. But we appreciate your time this morning. STEINFORT : Still plenty of time left in the day. JEFFREYS: Thank you for joining us. See you soon. E&OE Digital Duty of Care; Tobacco Excise; Raymond Terrace M1 Extension Share
